title: Agent observations with validity boundaries and preconditioned actions
description:
WHY: An agent clicking an old coordinate system is the automation version of the stale-click bug. Observations carry validity metadata; actions carry preconditions; violations refuse rather than guess.

SCOPE: Observation payloads: display geometry + generation, configuration generation, frame identity, source-freshness status, capture/presentation timestamps with uncertainty, current control authority; optional screenshots as user-requested artifacts bound to the producing observation, labeled by evidence level (decoded / submitted-to-compositor / instrumentally observed); actions accepting preconditions (expected geometry generation, current lease, maximum observation age) refused with typed reasons when stale — the client never auto-refreshes a precondition to repeat a potentially destructive action; window/focus preconditions labeled best-effort unless the platform is genuinely atomic; partial batch submission and unknown effects explicitly labeled; "submitted to OS" reported separately from "observed application result" (new pixels do not prove semantic success).

ACCEPTANCE: precondition-violation tests (geometry change between observe and act -> refusal); artifact-binding tests; an agent-driven e2e that survives a mid-task resize by re-observing rather than misclicking, fully logged. Provenance: plan section 18.2.

title: fr robot surface: JSON session/observe/input commands with staged acknowledgements
description:
WHY: Agents are first-class operators. The plan's command surface (fr hosts/status/doctor/inspect + fr robot session open/observe/input/close, frd status/approval/sharing) makes automation useful without an MCP server or workflow language — if the envelope is honest about what actually happened.

SCOPE: The robot envelope (schema version, timestamps, typed error code, specific next action) on every command; every response distinguishing success / partial submission / cancellation / refusal / unknown external effect; acknowledgement stages named admitted / submitted-to-OS / observed — never "exactly once"; an explicit robot session with view/control role returning status, limits, and an opaque local lease handle; commands reuse the live local client session (never a secret new host controller per input); the local client authenticates its caller — a handle printed on a command line is not authority, and bearer material stays out of argv and ordinary JSON; local-approval mode identical for humans and agents; automation cannot set host approval or sharing policy remotely; frd sharing set own-user|tailnet and frd approval set local|none as local-only commands.

ACCEPTANCE: schema-versioned golden JSON fixtures; partial-batch and unknown-effect cases each producible in tests with the correct disposition; a scripted agent drives open->observe->input->close against a real host with the full envelope log. Provenance: plan sections 18.1, v1.2 CLI addition.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): the human-facing CLI commands share this surface: fr hosts, fr connect <host> (launching/attaching the desktop client), fr status, fr inspect <host>, fr disconnect <host>, plus frd install/status — same envelope underneath with human-readable rendering on top, so the human and robot paths cannot drift. Tests: golden output for both renderings of the same state; fr connect end-to-end through the e2e harness.

title: Extension: optional true 4:4:4 precision mode (HEVC range extensions)
description:
WHY: 4:2:0 discards spatial chroma that high bitrate cannot restore; colored terminal text and thin diagram lines benefit from true 4:4:4 where BOTH endpoints genuinely support the range-extension profile. Optional, native-oriented, never a baseline prerequisite.

SCOPE: Capability negotiation treating encode, decode, GPU interop, and presentation support as four separate checks; hardware-path-only by default (no silent CPU fallback — enabling via CPU requires showing the user the performance envelope); operating-point integration with the controller; capability rows per GPU/driver.

CONSTRAINTS: bounded budget inside the contingency; independent off switch; never holds the baseline architecture hostage; disabled cleanly where any of the four checks fails.

ACCEPTANCE: side-by-side text-quality evidence at matched bitrate/latency; capability rows recorded; the mode ships only where all four checks pass. Provenance: plan sections 14.2, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Probe unit tests for all four capability checks (encode/decode/interop/present) with each failure combination producing its typed refusal

title: Extension: bounded HEVC-only chroma-carrier experiment
description:
WHY: A research extension carrying full-resolution chroma in the luma plane of an auxiliary ordinary HEVC stream — preserving the single-codec policy while changing the representation. A known technique family, not a claimed invention; plausibly the best text-color path where 4:4:4 hardware is absent.

SCOPE: Packed auxiliary-surface arrangement within encoder/decoder geometry limits; matching capture/configuration identities between base and auxiliary frames (never overlay stale chroma on newer luma); base view stays responsive while precision waits within a small bound or falls back explicitly; requires dependable access to decoded component samples with exact scaling/range semantics — endpoints exposing only color-converted RGB or opaque surfaces disable the extension; explicit coded-pixel and decoder-session cost accounting; not mathematically lossless and never claimed as such.

CONSTRAINTS: fixed portion of the contingency budget; ABANDON criteria binding — two-stream decode cost, color presentation, mobile thermals, or complexity outweighing the text benefit ends the experiment with a negative-evidence note.

ACCEPTANCE: working two-stream demo with correct reconstruction on at least one qualified pair, plus measured cost; or the documented abandonment. Provenance: plan sections 14.3, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for chroma packing/unpacking arithmetic; reconstruction correctness verified by image hash against a reference transform

title: Extension: authorized FrankenTerm semantic observation adapter
description:
WHY: When the shared application is FrankenTerm and the user explicitly grants the capability, agents can read actual pane text/state through ft robot instead of OCRing pixels — dramatically better agent ergonomics at zero cost to the baseline daemon.

SCOPE: Read-only pane observation as the initial semantic extension: restricted to the explicitly selected pane/session with visibility/authorization revalidated (a mux can hold hidden unrelated panes); the same session authorization path — never a bypass, never scope beyond the selected panes, never a general remote command execution endpoint; the full ft robot write/execute namespace NOT exposed; terminal output treated as untrusted application content; integration optional and outside the baseline daemon's dependency graph (a separate opt-in component); envelope schema reuse independent of granting terminal access.

ACCEPTANCE: an agent reads pane text through the adapter under explicit grant; revocation/visibility tests; dependency-graph check proving frd carries nothing from it by default. Provenance: plan sections 18.3, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every semantic read logged with pane identity and grant reference; audit log verified in tests

title: Extension: selective small-group RaptorQ FEC experiment
description:
WHY: Baseline repair is retransmission + reliable bootstrap (proven in Phase 1); RaptorQ over small fragment groups might beat it on lossy paths — but only measurement decides, and a failed recovery gate was never allowed to hide behind future FEC.

SCOPE: Existing asupersync RaptorQ machinery applied to small groups of media fragments on the datagram path; compare against the shipped repair under the impairment matrix on stall frequency, latency, repair bytes, and CPU; adoption only where it wins across the board on target hardware including mobile decode-side CPU.

CONSTRAINTS: bounded budget; independent off switch; never mandatory on every frame (explicitly rejected scope); loses cleanly if it complicates the recovery generations.

ACCEPTANCE: the comparison table with retained runs; adopt/abandon decision note either way. Provenance: plan sections 12.2, 23 extension lane, 25.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for group-coding boundaries; comparison harness runs scripted with retained logs per impairment row

title: fr-lab: deterministic scenario harness on the Asupersync lab
description:
WHY: The plan's correctness story rests on deterministic simulation of loss, reordering, delay, cancellation, and timer races against the PRODUCTION state machines — not generated traces that never touch production logic. This harness is the substrate for the Phase 1 property suite and for replaying controller decisions from sanitized traces later.

SCOPE: crates/fr-lab providing: deterministic transport adapters (drop/duplicate/reorder/delay by seed and schedule) that plug where real QUIC/WSS plug; virtual monotonic clocks including suspend/resume jumps and scheduler-stall injection; bounded-channel instrumentation that asserts byte budgets, not just queue length; a scenario builder that scripts host+client state machines through connect/view/control/fault/teardown sequences; failure output that logs the full event schedule and seed so any red run reproduces with one command.

CONSTRAINTS: Asupersync lab facilities only — no wall-clock sleeps, no real sockets in this crate. Real TLS/codec interop is explicitly out of scope here (native/browser lanes own it).

ACCEPTANCE: a demo scenario drives a toy state machine through loss+reorder deterministically twice with identical event logs; seed printed on every failure; harness API documented for the Phase 1 property-suite bead. Provenance: plan sections 4.1, 18.4, 24.1.

title: fr-wire: bounded binary framing, golden fixtures, fuzz seed corpus
description:
WHY: Every transport profile (QUIC, WebTransport, WSS) carries the same application messages; one bounded codec with goldens is the interoperability anchor and the first fuzz target.

SCOPE: crates/fr-wire implementing PROTOCOL.md v0: fixed header plus bounded length-delimited fields; no unconstrained object-graph deserialization; parse validity, negotiated capability, and authorization kept as SEPARATE check layers; every limit validated before constructing objects; unknown optional fields ignorable only under the bounded framing rule, unknown required flags fail closed; fragment metadata (total length, offset/index, count, stream binding, frame identity, recovery/configuration generation) with overlap/conflict rejection where identical duplicates are harmless. Golden fixture files checked into the repo for every message class — byte-exact, versioned — plus a fuzz harness seed corpus grown from them.

CONSTRAINTS: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. No serde-ecosystem sprawl; the smallest utilities that pass the dependency doctrine. All arithmetic checked.

ACCEPTANCE: round-trip tests for every message; golden bytes stable across runs (goldens never regenerated to force green — a golden change requires an explicit protocol-version rationale in the commit); negative tests for truncation, overlap, oversize, unknown-required, wrong-role; fuzz target builds and runs clean for a smoke duration in CI lanes with detailed failure logging (input hex + parse trace). Provenance: plan sections 12.4, 17.1, 17.2.

title: Image clipboard as a negotiated optional capability over the transfer channel
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes text clipboard sync default-on; image clipboard (screenshots, copied figures) is the natural next expectation. It is explicitly a NEGOTIATED optional capability carried over the bounded file-transfer channel — never smuggled through the 64 KiB control parser — so it must not be lost as a feature nor allowed to bloat the core clipboard path.

SCOPE: Negotiate image-clipboard capability per session; carry image payloads (PNG canonical form; size-capped, initial ceiling 16 MiB) over the ATP-backed transfer channel with the same budgets and atomic-publication rules; host/client clipboard integration per OS (respecting the Linux portal grant, macOS pasteboard types, Windows CF_DIB/PNG round-trip); the same echo-loop prevention, controller-only scope, approval gating, and never-logged rules as text; decode of received images treated as untrusted input (bounded dimensions/pixels before any decode, reusing the fr-core limit arithmetic).

ACCEPTANCE: copy-image-both-directions e2e on all three host OSes with format round-trip verification by content hash; oversized/hostile-image refusal tests (decompression-bomb fixtures); capability row recorded per platform; logs show transfer metadata only, never pixels. Provenance: plan section 15.3 (v1.4).

title: Phase 0 gate: Chrome and Safari HEVC WebCodecs decode-and-present probe at real geometry
description:
WHY: WebCodecs does not mandate HEVC; support is per browser/OS/hardware combination. The v1.3 decision makes current Chrome and Safari (on combinations where their HEVC path passes) the browser qualification bar — this spike determines what that bar actually covers, before the browser client is built.

SCOPE: In real Chrome and Safari on their supported OS/hardware: generate the complete HEVC codec identifier from actual stream configuration (hvc1/hev1 parameter-set rules consistent with the bytes, 4-byte-length-prefixed NALs in complete access units, exact hvcC); VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported followed by REAL decode-and-present of a representative sequence at real display geometry. Test specifically: a single IDR; one P picture after long idle; the final frame of a burst (some paths retain output when no more frames arrive); recovery after loss; low-cadence presentation. Never call flush() per frame (the flush algorithm requires the next chunk to be a key chunk). Close VideoFrame objects promptly; bound decodeQueueSize AND renderer retention; prefer worker-based decoding where supported. Record hardware-vs-software decode evidence per combination.

ACCEPTANCE: a written support matrix (browser x OS x hardware -> passed/failed/blocked/not tested) with capture of the probe outputs; the emitted-bitstream requirements this imposes on host encoders. Failure meaning: narrow the matrix honestly; no second codec, no per-frame flush hacks. Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 16.3, 23 Phase 0, v1.3 note in section 1.

title: Decision notes: FFmpeg binding family, desktop windowing/shell, mobile FFI mechanism
description:
WHY: The plan bounds three implementation choices as short evidence-based decisions, explicitly forbidding open-ended adapter competitions: the exact FFmpeg wrapper revision, the native GUI/windowing binding, and (per v1.4) the Swift/Kotlin binding mechanism for the shared core.

SCOPE: Three short decision notes, each citing spike evidence: (1) FFmpeg binding — default expectation is a pinned ffmpeg-sys-next-family binding under the project-owned interface, with ffmpeg-next and ffmpeg-the-third evaluated during the build spike; one family chosen, one FFmpeg ABI qualified; no competing wrapper maintained. (2) Desktop windowing/shell — one minimal maintained integration preserving hardware-surface presentation per OS (AppKit/Metal, Win32/D3D, a Linux layer), chosen for surface interop, with accessibility/DPI/input/lifecycle costs counted in the client budget; no Electron/Chromium. (3) Mobile FFI — hand-written C ABI plus maintained Swift package / Kotlin JNI wrapper, or a qualified binding generator; chosen for auditability of the narrow boundary, keeping all logic in Rust.

ACCEPTANCE: each note states the decision, the evidence rows it rests on, the rejected alternatives with one-line reasons, and the revisit condition. Committed under docs/. Provenance: plan sections 9.1, 16.1, 16.2, 25.

title: Phase 0 spike: Linux PipeWire portal -> VAAPI/NVENC HEVC -> decode -> present
description:
WHY: Wayland capture is portal-mediated and DMA-BUF-based; sharing a file descriptor is not synchronization. Buffer ownership, modifiers, plane layout, fences, and cache sync must be handled explicitly, and compositors differ enough that GNOME, KDE, and wlroots-family are separate qualification rows.

SCOPE: Spike: ScreenCast portal session -> PipeWire stream (resolve stream by the strongest identifier offered — recent portal versions expose a PipeWire serial because node IDs are reused) -> GPU-local copy into an owned surface where the compositor buffer cannot be held -> FFmpeg VAAPI (and NVENC where present) HEVC encode -> hardware decode -> native presentation. Clear padding/cropped borders in newly allocated surfaces so stale GPU contents can never become encoded pixels. Run on at least GNOME and KDE; record wlroots-family status even if only as blocked/not-tested.

MEASURE: the standard set (first packet, steady delay, copies, IDR verification, config readback) per compositor row, plus DMA-BUF import/export paths actually used and fence behavior.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible command + exact compositor/portal/driver versions per row + results + retained failure reasons. Failure narrows the Linux support matrix honestly rather than adding a hidden CPU path. Provenance: plan sections 8.3, 10.1, 11.1, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 spike: macOS ScreenCaptureKit -> VideoToolbox HEVC -> decode -> present
description:
WHY: The entire product premise on Apple hardware — capture surface to hardware HEVC to hardware decode to GPU presentation with pixels staying on the GPU — must be proven as a small real vertical experiment before any architecture is built around it. Apple's documented low-latency VideoToolbox rate-control mode is H.264-specific; HEVC needs its OWN real-time, hardware-required, no-reordering configuration and measurement.

SCOPE: A standalone spike (spikes/, not crates/) on Apple Silicon: ScreenCaptureKit full-display capture -> (GPU color conversion only if needed) -> VideoToolbox HEVC encode (Main 8-bit 4:2:0, low-delay I/P, no reordering, no lookahead, one previous reference where allowed) -> VideoToolbox decode -> Metal/native-layer presentation. Drive it with a representative desktop-sized moving/text workload, never only a tiny synthetic frame.

MEASURE AND RECORD: time-to-first-packet, steady-state encode delay, decode delay, copy count along the path (zero-copy is a measured property, not a claim), reconfiguration latency, verified independently-decodable IDR on start/reconfigure (observe the emitted bitstream, including effective reorder/reference requirements — an API accepting a request proves nothing), effective configuration readback, behavior at low cadence and after long idle.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible command + exact hardware/OS/driver identity + results + retained failure reasons checked into the spike directory. Failure meaning: revisit surface interop/backend choice before building the GUI around it. Provenance: plan sections 8.1-8.3, 10.2, 11.1, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 spike: Windows Desktop Duplication -> FFmpeg hardware HEVC -> decode -> D3D present
description:
WHY: The Windows path runs through a trimmed FFmpeg libavcodec/libavutil boundary to NVENC/AMF/QSV; GPU-surface interop, capture formats, and hybrid-GPU laptops (capture on one adapter, encode on another) are exactly where hardware advantages die. Prove the pipeline before committing to it.

SCOPE: Spike on at least one qualified Windows GPU: Desktop Duplication capture (with cursor and dirty-region info, prompt frame release, copy-to-owned-surface when retention would block capture) -> D3D11 texture into an FFmpeg hardware encoder (whichever of NVENC/AMF/QSV the test machine has) -> hardware decode -> D3D presentation. Exercise access-lost, device-removed, resize, and duplication-session exhaustion. Note DuplicateOutput1 format behavior for HDR-to-SDR handling. Wrapper code must implement FFmpeg's real send/receive state machine: drain output for progress, retain reference-counted inputs until ownership permits reuse, distinguish EAGAIN/EOF/device-loss/fatal — never one-packet-per-frame assumptions or sleep-retry.

MEASURE: same set as the macOS spike (first packet, steady delay, copies, IDR verification, config readback), plus capture-device-vs-display-adapter mismatch behavior.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible command + exact GPU/driver/OS build identity + results + retained failure reasons. Feeds the FFmpeg-binding decision note. Provenance: plan sections 8.3, 9.1, 10.3, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: curated FFmpeg builds, signing, and native packaging spike
description:
WHY: The FFmpeg build nightmare is avoided by reducing the build, and licensing depends on configuration. Reproducible curated artifacts with recorded provenance are a release gate; discovering ABI/signing/licensing problems at release time is not acceptable.

SCOPE: Produce a curated FFmpeg distribution per needed desktop target with an explicit allowlist of required HEVC components and hardware integrations only — codecs, parsers, hardware contexts, bitstream normalization actually exercised; no muxers/demuxers/protocols/filters/executables. Build on matching builders; record compiler versions, source hashes, configuration arguments, checksums, license notices. The default hardware bundle avoids --enable-gpl/--enable-nonfree. Test the STRIPPED build itself against the media spikes. Verify dynamic-link loading from protected package paths only (no cwd/user-controlled search paths). macOS: sign/notarize a minimal process family and confirm permission attribution survives. Record the per-target component manifest and the distribution/licensing decision inputs (this bead records; the legal decision is the release gate).

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible build recipes committed under native/ with manifests; stripped artifacts pass the spike pipelines; signing walkthrough documented with evidence. Provenance: plan sections 9.2, 9.3, 20.2, 20.3, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: OS permission and lifecycle spikes (Wayland tokens, macOS TCC attribution, Windows session/loopback, lock/suspend)
description:
WHY: A daemon cannot erase OS consent boundaries, and permission attribution is packaging-dependent. Discovering these rules after the product is built is how remote-desktop projects die; the plan requires exact capability rows per OS before the architecture hardens.

SCOPE: Wayland: full portal sequence (create RemoteDesktop session, select devices/sources, request clipboard integration BEFORE Start, complete response, obtain restricted PipeWire remote and input connection); restore-token single-use rotation with atomic persistence; returned grants (not requested flags) determine authorization; session agent retains the portal session while delegating only the stream capability to a worker — a worker must never inherit input authority. macOS: signed launchd process family; Screen Recording + Accessibility permission attribution stable across updates and helper layout; protected-content reporting; sleep/wake and fast user switching. Windows: service vs interactive-agent split; Session 0 never treated as the user's desktop; lock/secure-desktop transitions as capability changes; SendInput integrity limits; WASAPI render-endpoint loopback scope (cross-session audio — must be disclosed, never misrepresented as per-user isolation). All platforms: lock/logout/user-switch ends observation and control; suspend/resume as an authority generation boundary.

ACCEPTANCE: a capability row table per OS (capture, pointer, keyboard, restore, clipboard, playback audio) with exact versions and passed/failed/blocked/not-tested; retained scripts; failure reasons. Provenance: plan sections 5.3, 10.1-10.3, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: qualify one live Asupersync QUIC endpoint composition end to end
description:
WHY: The inspected Asupersync tree exposes a native QUIC alias, but NativeQuicConnection performs no socket I/O, endpoint_api.rs explicitly declines to claim external interoperability, and adapter queues are not a deployable transport. Treating a type alias as a transport is the single largest architectural risk in the plan. This gate decides the native profile.

SCOPE: Choose ONE documented live endpoint composition and qualify its complete packet path: real UDP sockets suspending through the runtime's OS reactor (verify actual suspension per target, not async-looking signatures); TLS 1.3 certificate/hostname verification; negotiated project ALPN; packet protection; stream + DATAGRAM behavior including negotiated DATAGRAM size limits (QUIC's 1200-byte minimum Initial is NOT 1200 bytes of datagram payload; Tailscale's MTU is 1280); retransmission, congestion accounting, pacing; multi-client routing; cancellation; bounded allocations. Interoperate against an INDEPENDENT QUIC/H3 peer in the test harness (test-only dependency, never shipped). Test direct and forced-DERP-relay paths. Loopback tests that manually advance handshake states are not security evidence.

FAILURE MEANING: keep the unqualified path disabled; count bounded upstream Asupersync work against the 15k transport allowance; qualify and label the WSS profile instead. NEVER implement a second QUIC stack or import another runtime.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible commands, captured interop transcripts, measured behavior under loss, and a written go/no-go with evidence. Provenance: plan sections 4.1, 12.1, 12.4, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: fragmented HEVC loss recovery and authority-expiry spike
description:
WHY: With 1100-byte payloads, a 50 KiB access unit spans 47 datagrams (37.6% chance of losing at least one at 1% independent loss) and a 1 MiB IDR spans 954 (loss near-certain), and 1 MiB takes about 1.68 s to serialize at 5 Mbps. "Drop and send another IDR" is not viable; the recovery design must be proven against real fragmented HEVC before any low-latency claim exists.

SCOPE: A spike combining the wire fragmentation format, deterministic loss/reorder injection, and real encoded HEVC: sender fragment cache bounded by bytes and time; receiver coalesced missing-range requests after a small reordering allowance, clamped in range/retries/frequency/bytes; separate DISPLAY deadline vs REFERENCE-retention deadline (repair a too-old-to-display picture only while it unlocks dependents within the horizon, initial estimate ceil(fps x horizon)+2 pictures, horizon <= 250 ms, clamped to the negotiated 2-12 window and byte budget); dedicated bounded reliable stream for startup/recovery IDRs; only one outstanding recovery per pipeline; the non-circular startup handshake (DecoderConfiguration -> DecoderConfigured [API configured, not first frame] -> RecoveryAccessUnit -> FirstFrameDecoded/PresentedState). Also: queue input through a long stall and prove expired actions do NOT execute afterward, and local revoke fences immediately.

ACCEPTANCE: bounded bytes/metadata asserted (not just queue lengths); stall/recovery behavior measured across loss patterns including a lost final fragment before idle; retained numbers. Failure meaning: no low-latency or safe-control operating point may be claimed. Provenance: plan sections 12.2-12.4, 15.1, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: Tailscale identity, membership, scope, and ingress qualification with real fixtures
description:
WHY: The entire authentication story is tailnet admission — FrankenRemote deliberately has no second credential. Same-tailnet membership, user identity for the v1.2 own-user default scope, and actual tunnel ingress must be POSITIVELY provable from the installed Tailscale's authenticated local metadata on tested versions, or admission must refuse.

SCOPE: Qualify LocalAPI/status/WhoIs access per platform installation variant (Linux socket, Windows local transport, macOS Standalone/App Store/CLI). Build real fixtures: two local members with different owners; a tagged member; a shared-in host; an external sharee; a user present in more than one tailnet; a TAGGED HOST (which has no owning user and therefore cannot use the own-user default — must force explicit scope selection). Verify: source address must be one of the node's own addresses (not behind a subnet route); ShareeNode/AltSharerUserID/Sharer interpretation; InNetworkMap alone proves nothing; DNS suffixes/zero-valued sharer fields/email-domain equality are NOT authorization; IPv4+IPv6 ingress binding to tailnet addresses with platform firewall/interface enforcement; behavior on local identity change, key expiry, and policy removal. Missing/ambiguous evidence -> typed refusal tailnet_membership_unverifiable; the app-capability-grant profile is the configured alternative, never an ad hoc allowlist.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture results per Tailscale version/variant recorded; the exact metadata fields the adapter may rely on pinned with their tested semantics; scope-check (own-user vs tailnet) decisions demonstrated against the fixtures. Provenance: plan sections 6.1-6.3, 19.2, 23 Phase 0, v1.2 note.

title: Phase 0 spike: host virtual-microphone endpoint per OS (PipeWire source, CoreAudio plugin, Windows driver)
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes audio bidirectional. Client-to-host microphone requires a host-side virtual input device that real applications can select; this is trivial on Linux, signed user-space plugin work on macOS, and genuine driver-class work on Windows. The risk must be retired before mic forwarding is promised per OS.

SCOPE: Per OS, create a selectable input device and route a test Opus uplink into a real host application (e.g., a recorder or meeting app): Linux — PipeWire virtual source; macOS — signed user-space CoreAudio server plugin (BlackHole-style architecture; validate the signing/packaging path and TCC interaction); Windows — signed virtual audio endpoint driver (evaluate: own driver vs a vetted existing open component with recorded provenance; either way, it is native non-Rust code counted like other native artifacts, with its own signing chain). Measure added latency per endpoint and device-change behavior.

CONSTRAINTS: no undisclosed third-party driver downloads; where an endpoint cannot be qualified, microphone forwarding ships as a TYPED UNSUPPORTED capability on that host OS — never a fake device.

ACCEPTANCE: per-OS row (created device, app-visible, audio flowed, latency measured, signing path validated) with passed/failed/blocked status and retained evidence; a recommendation for the Windows approach with licensing/provenance notes. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 23 Phase 0 (v1.4 row).

title: Phase 0 gate: real HTTP/3 WebTransport interop with Chrome (and Safari where available) plus WSS fallback shape
description:
WHY: A queued adapter or self-loopback is not interoperability. The browser profile requires an actual browser completing the HTTP/3/WebTransport handshake against the production-intended listener, and the WSS fallback needs its bounded-credit shape proven early because browser WebSocket has no application receive backpressure.

SCOPE: Against the qualified (or candidate) Asupersync H3 endpoint: real negotiated SETTINGS, extended CONNECT session establishment, HTTP Datagram association, stream prefixes, required capsule handling; pin the exact WebTransport draft/implementation compatibility tested. Datagram size budget computed from inner MTU 1280 minus IP/UDP/QUIC/WebTransport overheads — measure the actual usable payload. Exercise session binding, cancellation, reconnect, and origin-checked establishment. Chrome is the primary target; record Safari WebTransport status (expected gap: Safari may need the WSS profile — that is an accepted, labeled outcome under the v1.3 Chrome+Safari qualification bar). For WSS: prove separately-bound channels, receiver-granted outstanding-byte credit (bufferedAmount reports outbound buffering only), and stale-generation fencing on channel replacement.

ACCEPTANCE: transcript of a real browser handshake + datagram exchange with the tested draft/version pinned; measured payload budget; WSS credit protocol demonstrated; go/no-go with evidence. Failure meaning: label WSS as the browser profile and publish the tested H3 status honestly. Provenance: plan sections 12.1, 12.4, 12.5, 16.4, 23 Phase 0.

title: Adaptive quality controller v0: deterministic, hysteretic, pressure-aware
description:
WHY: Phase 1 needs basic rate control that never oscillates and never mistakes encoder stalls for network pressure; the sophisticated tuning is Phase 4, but the deterministic skeleton and measurement honesty land here.

SCOPE: A deterministic controller with hysteresis, bounded step sizes, and minimum dwell times; separate pressure attribution (network vs encoder vs decoder vs presentation) before any setting changes; reduce offered load fast on persistent queue growth, increase slowly after sustained headroom; budget includes keyframes, retransmissions, auxiliary data, audio, and per-viewer shares with a per-host/per-path aggregate ceiling; provisional operating points near 75-85% of a measured sustainable delivery estimate, never from momentary spikes; application-limited samples marked (idle screens are not low link capacity); unknown metrics recorded as unknown, never derived certainty; conservative restart after idle/route-change/reconnect; bounded probe bursts only when queues are healthy; reconfiguration via announced new generation at a clean recovery point unless the backend has a qualified low-stall in-place path; path-change resets estimates.

ACCEPTANCE: controller decisions are a pure function of its logged inputs (replayable — this is the hook Phase 4 diagnostics builds on); lab scenarios for step response, oscillation damping, and pressure misattribution; every decision logged with its input snapshot. Provenance: plan sections 13.1-13.4.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for step/hysteresis/dwell functions; every decision log entry carries its full input snapshot for replay

title: First desktop client shell: window, hardware-surface presentation, input capture, minimal toolbar
description:
WHY: Phase 1 ends with a human actually using a remote desktop; that requires one real native shell over fr-client, built on the windowing decision note, presenting decoded frames without GPU-to-CPU readback.

SCOPE: For the chosen first client OS: window/session lifecycle, hardware decode output to a native presentation surface (VideoToolbox layer / D3D swapchain per the decision), keyboard and pointer capture including modifier and focus-loss semantics feeding fr-client's sequencing, minimal UI (machine picker fed by discovery-lite or manual FQDN, connect/disconnect, display choice, connection-state indicator, revoke-visible state), local cursor rendering with the single-owner rule, DPI/scale correctness (native pixels when practical, one explicit scaling step), clean teardown releasing held input state.

CONSTRAINTS: no web platform, no Electron; accessibility/DPI/input/lifecycle costs counted in the client budget; presentation path preserves the measured copy discipline.

ACCEPTANCE: a human drives a real remote session end to end; focus loss releases input state (verified in logs); resize and display-scale changes reject stale coordinates until the new geometry generation is acknowledged; e2e script exercising connect/control/revoke/reconnect with screenshots and full logs. Provenance: plan sections 14.1, 16.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests for coordinate/DPI/scale mapping and focus-loss release logic; e2e script logs every input disposition
- [ ] Shortcut-capture toggle: a mode that routes system-reserved shortcuts to the remote desktop where the client OS allows it, advertised as a per-platform capability row (plan 15.1); toggle state visible in the toolbar and logged

title: fr-e2e: scripted end-to-end session harness with structured logging and artifact capture
description:
WHY: Every feature bead's acceptance names e2e scenarios; without one shared harness those become ad-hoc shell scripts with inconsistent logging and no artifact retention. This harness is the runnable spine for all of them — the consumer is every feature bead from Phase 1 on, and the phase gates' fault suites execute through it.

SCOPE: A harness (under fr-lab or a sibling test crate plus scripts/e2e/) that: launches a real frd process family and a real client core (headless client driver first; desktop-shell driving where the platform permits) against a loopback or real tailnet endpoint; scripts scenarios as data (connect, authorize, view, control, inject faults, tear down); captures STRUCTURED logs from every process (host authority transitions, queue depths, per-action input dispositions, recovery events) into a per-run artifact directory with the exact commit, config, and seed; standard fault injectors (kill/stall worker, drop transport, expire tickets, resize display) reusable across scenarios; assertion helpers over the captured logs (e.g. "no input executed after revoke", "queue high-water under N bytes"); every red run reproducible from its artifact bundle with one command.

CONSTRAINTS: real processes and real transports — no mocks presented as live proof; deterministic-lab scenarios stay in fr-lab (this harness is the real-process complement); scenario registration convention documented so each feature bead lands at least one scenario with itself.

ACCEPTANCE: the harness runs a connect/control/revoke/reconnect scenario against the Phase 1 pair with full artifacts; a planted violation (deliberately delayed revoke fence in a test build) is caught by the assertion layer, proving the harness can fail; CI lane wiring documented. Provenance: plan sections 23 Phase 1 gate, 24.2; AGENTS section 7 (evidence discipline).

title: fr-ffi: FFmpeg hardware codec wrapper behind the media contracts (Windows/Linux)
description:
WHY: Windows and Linux hardware HEVC run through a trimmed FFmpeg libavcodec/libavutil boundary (NVENC/AMF/QSV/VAAPI). This is the project's largest unsafe/foreign surface; it lives in one audited crate behind the fr-media contracts so nothing FFmpeg-shaped ever leaks upward, and so the macOS path never waits on it.

SCOPE: crates/fr-ffi implementing the fr-media Encoder/Decoder contracts over the pinned binding family from the Phase 0 decision note, against the curated FFmpeg build: the REAL send/receive state machine — drain available output to make progress, never assume one packet per submitted frame, never sleep-retry EAGAIN; retain reference-counted inputs until ownership permits reuse; distinguish temporary backpressure, EOF, device loss, and fatal corruption as typed results; end-of-stream draining kept off the per-frame path; compressed input buffers with the alignment/padding the native API requires, allocated via the library's packet/buffer facilities with checked lengths and initialized padding — never a raw unpadded network slice; timestamps, duration, output status, color information, and configuration changes preserved through the wrapper; configure/encode/decode calls off the authority/event-loop thread; all callback contexts and GPU resources alive until completion or contained worker termination; GPU surfaces opaque, hardware-context handling audited; documented pointer provenance, callback threading, buffer ownership, and shutdown order per AGENTS section 3.2.

CONSTRAINTS: one binding family only (no competing wrapper); FFmpeg types never appear in fr-media/session/wire signatures; libraries load from protected package paths only.

ACCEPTANCE: integration tests against the curated build exercising backpressure, drain, device-loss, and hostile-input paths with full state-transition logging; sanitizer lanes (ASan/UBSan where the target permits) green; fuzz the compressed-input boundary with the padded-allocation contract asserted; a leak test across 10k encode/decode cycles. Provenance: plan sections 9.1, 9.2, 19.1.

title: fr-client: shared client session core (connect, decode scheduling, freshness, input sequencing, reconnect)
description:
WHY: One Rust core drives desktop, mobile, and browser clients; platform shells stay logic-thin. This crate is that core, and everything the v1.4 mobile apps and the WASM build reuse.

SCOPE: crates/fr-client: connection establishment against fr-transport with certificate/destination verification; session state machine mirroring host authority (never assuming control from media arrival); decoder scheduling honoring reference dependencies with bounded queues; presentation policy — newest ready frame wins, obsolete presentation work discarded, decoded-vs-presented progress reported separately (background/occluded rendering never counts as presentation); view-freshness tracking that suspends input readiness on sustained unknown/stale presentation while read-only diagnostics continue; client-side input capture semantics (ordered actions vs replaceable pointer states, separate sequence spaces, click coordinate barriers, relative checkpoints); reconnect flow — media reconnect may preserve viewing but NEVER silently restores a revoked input lease; a fresh lease and recovery point on resume; viewport/mapping model distinguishing local zoom (client transform only) from host crop (negotiated mapping generation, acknowledged before coordinate input uses it); diagnostics surface.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests plus lab-driven integration covering reconnect-without-lease-resurrection, stale-view input suspension, and mapping-generation rejection of stale coordinates, with full state-trace logging. Provenance: plan sections 7.1-7.3, 11.3, 14.4, 16.1.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Auto-reconnect with bounded backoff and a user-visible reconnecting state; reconnect attempts and outcomes logged; control re-request only after view freshness is re-established (never silent lease resurrection)

title: fr-media: safe media contracts, capability probing, and the baseline bitstream rules
description:
WHY: FrankenRemote owns the interface, not the codec. A small ownership-aware contract keeps every backend replaceable and keeps codec library types out of session and wire layers forever. This bead is deliberately CONTRACTS-ONLY and depends on nothing platform-specific: the macOS VideoToolbox path consumes these contracts directly, so the Phase 1 Apple vertical is never blocked behind the Windows/Linux FFmpeg binding decision (that wrapper is its own bead, fr-ffi).

SCOPE: crates/fr-media (safe, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]): Encoder, Decoder, GpuSurface (opaque), EncodedAccessUnit, CodecConfiguration, MediaCapabilities; capability probing that encodes/decodes a real representative workload and reads back effective configuration (an API accepting a request proves nothing); probe caching keyed by OS/driver/device identity, invalidated on device loss; live-session admission against current capacity; observable copy counting per path; the baseline bitstream contract every backend must satisfy: HEVC Main 8-bit 4:2:0, no frame reordering, low-delay I/P with one previous reference where allowed, bounded decoded-picture buffering, verified independently-decodable IDR on startup/reconfigure/recovery, provisional max GOP 2 s during ACTIVE encoding only (never waking a static screen), coded dimensions advertised separately from visible crop with initialized padding, SDR default with explicit color primaries/transfer/matrix/range, qualified HDR-to-SDR tone-map or typed refusal (clipped HDR is never labeled SDR support); hardware-required means fail or explicitly select a software profile — never a silent library-internal fallback.

ACCEPTANCE: contract unit tests with a scriptable fake backend (including probe-cache invalidation and admission refusal paths); compile-time/API-review test that no foreign codec type appears in any public fr-media signature; detailed probe logging (device identity, effective config, copy counts). Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 8.2, 9.1.

title: fr-tailnet: LocalAPI identity adapter, admission policy, scope enforcement, ingress binding
description:
WHY: Implements the qualified identity evidence from the Phase 0 gate as the production admission path. The admission policy IS the authentication story.

SCOPE: crates/fr-tailnet: narrow Rust client for the installed Tailscale LocalAPI (or the qualified platform bridge — bounded CLI invocation at setup/admission where that is the supported path; never a shell with peer-supplied arguments, never per-packet subprocesses); internally consistent status/WhoIs snapshots with retry on local identity change; the full admission conjunction — verified current same-tailnet node AND within the locally selected sharing scope (default: nodes of the host's own tailnet user; explicit option: all members/tags) AND allowed by Tailscale policy AND locally enabled sharing AND capability supported AND controller slot AND approval when configured; typed refusals for every failure including tailnet_membership_unverifiable; binding each connection's transport peer address to node identity (own addresses only, not subnet-routed); listeners bound only to current tailnet node addresses with platform ingress enforcement; revalidation on path change; disabled replayable early data; subscription to local Tailscale changes — when identity authority is unavailable, admit nothing new, stop renewing, terminate at recorded deadlines; tagged-host handling (no owning user -> explicit scope selection required); the app-capability grant profile as configured alternative.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests against recorded fixture data from the Phase 0 identity gate (different owners, tagged, shared-in, sharee, multi-tailnet); scope decisions logged with the exact evidence used; e2e smoke against a real tailnet. Provenance: plan sections 6.1-6.3, v1.2 note.

title: fr-transport: qualified native QUIC integration with channel semantics and packet budgets
description:
WHY: Turns the Phase 0 transport qualification into the production native profile with the plan's traffic partition, so input can never queue behind bulk bytes and datagrams carry only replaceable media.

SCOPE: crates/fr-transport over the ONE qualified Asupersync endpoint composition: reliable ordered channels for critical input and small session operations; separate bounded channels for clipboard, configuration, cursor shapes, and the bootstrap/recovery stream; datagrams for video access-unit fragments, audio, replaceable pointer state; the file-transfer channel as its own bounded stream class (budgeted, never ahead of input on a shared resource); connection-level flow-control credit reserved for control so bulk cannot starve key-up; payload budget computed from inner MTU 1280 minus IP/UDP/QUIC-protection/DATAGRAM-frame/application-header overheads, qualified on IPv4 and IPv6; no IP fragmentation reliance; compact negotiated stream bindings (session/display/codec-config/recovery/viewport) so datagrams reject stale work cheaply; per-turn poll work limits so codec feedback cannot starve the reactor; 0-RTT application operations disabled.

ACCEPTANCE: integration tests over the lab adapters plus real-socket loopback; budget arithmetic unit-tested against both IP versions; a saturation test proving input latency stays bounded while bulk channels are full, with logged per-channel queue depths. Provenance: plan sections 12.1, 12.4, 15.6.

title: Frame pipeline and freshness contract: bounded queues, two ages, cursor/damage, idle
description:
WHY: This is differentiator number one — optimize the age of useful state, not throughput. Every stage gets a bounded queue and a defined rule for obsolete work that respects codec references.

SCOPE: Host and client pipeline policy per the plan's queue table: one replaceable latest pending capture; one-or-two in-flight encoder surfaces where the backend allows (admitting a driver's real requirement only after memory+latency accounting); byte+deadline-limited compressed outbound; negotiated reassembly window (2-12 units by count AND bytes); bounded decoder queue respecting references; newest-frame presentation; small strict audio jitter ceiling. Hidden stages count: codec-internal surfaces, packet caches, QUIC send buffers, renderer-held frames, shared-viewer retention — physical allocations accounted once, each subscriber charged for work it can force; a stalled viewer cannot pin unbounded shared history. "Skip presentation" separated from "discard reference state"; never free driver-owned surfaces to satisfy a metric. Two ages tracked distinctly: last pixel update vs last trustworthy source observation (serviced capture op, OS-qualified damage/unchanged evidence, or unknown — with bounded verification capture at a declared cadence where cheap evidence is impossible, cost reported); stale marking while heartbeats stay healthy. Cursor: shape reliable, position replaceable, single rendering owner via capability bit, unknown-shape fallback, no double cursor in pointer-lock/touch modes. Damage: full valid surface reconstruction before full-frame encode (dirty rects are not permission to encode uninitialized pixels); surface clearing after resize/device loss. Idle: stationary screens stop transmission except refresh/refinement, first damage exits idle promptly, source-verification distinguishes idle from hung capture.

ACCEPTANCE: lab property tests for every bound (bytes and counts) with planted violations; an e2e soak on the real macOS path logging queue high-water marks and both ages; static-screen test proving near-zero encode work while freshness evidence continues. Provenance: plan sections 3.1, 11.1-11.4, 13.4.

title: frd broker: idle daemon, listeners, session registry, role-capability IPC, process family
description:
WHY: The always-running piece must be small, idle-cheap, and incapable of media work by construction — the proposed idle envelope is under 25 MiB RSS and under 0.1% of one core with NO capture, encoder, or GPU surfaces resident.

SCOPE: crates/frd: tailnet listeners (from fr-tailnet/fr-transport/fr-certs), small local configuration (sharing scope own-user/tailnet, approval mode, selected session/displays, audio/file settings), current peer-identity cache, session registry, browser-asset serving stub, local control socket; the internal process-role family (broker / interactive-session agent / media worker) as modes of a signed process family; local IPC with parent-created or protected endpoints, OS peer credentials where available, ROLE-SPECIFIC capabilities and process/session generations — credentials alone identify a user, not a trusted helper; workers receive no Tailscale control socket, no certificate keys, no approval endpoint, no input-lease capability; privileged platform broker kept minimal (service registration, user-session launch, protected Tailscale metadata/cert ops) with no arbitrary privileged RPC; startup before login where the OS supports it, honestly reporting when no shareable desktop exists.

ACCEPTANCE: idle measurement harness (process-family RSS/CPU over a defined quiet interval) with results recorded against the envelope; IPC forgery unit tests (wrong role, wrong generation, unauthorized user) all refused with typed errors and logs. Provenance: plan sections 5.1, 5.2, 19.2, 21.1.

title: First host adapter: macOS ScreenCaptureKit capture + VideoToolbox encode in the media worker role
description:
WHY: Phase 1 needs one complete real host. Apple Silicon is the preferred first path (spike-proven), keeping capture and encode co-located in an on-demand worker so GPU surfaces never cross processes and a hung codec cannot touch authority.

SCOPE: Productionize the macOS spike inside the media-worker process role: SCK full-display capture with borrowed-buffer discipline (owned GPU copy at the documented release point), cursor capture mode and damage metadata where granted, VideoToolbox HEVC session with the qualified real-time no-reordering configuration, encoded access units + bounded metadata to the broker over bounded IPC; worker lifecycle — spawn on demand, generation-fenced teardown, kill-on-stall with authority fencing FIRST, restart with bounded rate/backoff, repeated GPU failure ends the media profile rather than spawning unlimited workers; explicit thread affinity for SCK callbacks and VT completions; permission loss / display removal / display-color changes as typed capability events; protected-content reported as such, never as a stalled network.

ACCEPTANCE: runs as the real process family on Apple Silicon; kill -9 of the worker mid-encode leaves broker+agent healthy and the next session admits cleanly; e2e script capturing a moving desktop for minutes with logged queue depths, copy counts, and zero unbounded growth. Provenance: plan sections 5.4, 10.2, 11.1.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for worker lifecycle state machine; the fr-media fake-backend contract-conformance suite runs against this adapter

title: Tailscale HTTPS certificates: provisioning, renewal, atomic replacement, endpoint configuration
description:
WHY: TLS 1.3 underlies QUIC and browser trust; Tailscale-provisioned certificates for the host's tailnet FQDN are the only identity material — no second CA, no TOFU, no accept-any-certificate path ever, including under expiry pressure.

SCOPE: Certificate acquisition through the qualified Tailscale metadata/cert bridge (helper restricted to approved hostnames and protected key storage — not a general Tailscale admin proxy); renewal with backoff, pre-expiry alerts, continued use of a still-valid cert during renewal outages; ATOMIC install of chain+key; device rename / tailnet switch revalidates endpoint names before new sessions; one configurable unprivileged service port (8443 provisional default) for TCP and UDP with collision detection and honest endpoint reporting — never silently overwriting another listener or Tailscale Serve config; ALPN separation (project-native ALPN vs h3); setup reports tailnet-HTTPS enablement as an explicit prerequisite including certificate-transparency visibility of the machine name.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for rotation/atomicity/rename paths; a renewal-outage simulation proving still-valid certs keep serving and expiry never enables skip-verification; setup/doctor output naming the real endpoint. Provenance: plan sections 6.5, 20.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Renewal, rotation, and failure events logged with typed reasons and surfaced in fr doctor with expiry countdown

title: Input pipeline: ordered actions, tickets at submission, held-state cleanup, no replay
description:
WHY: Reliability is not permission to execute stale actions. This bead implements the complete input discipline that makes FrankenRemote safe for humans and mandatory for agents.

SCOPE: End to end across client core, wire, broker, session agent: one ordered bounded action sequence per lease (key/button transitions, scroll, committed text, mode changes); replaceable absolute pointer states on datagrams with their own sequence space (pointer gaps never create action-sequence gaps); click carries its coordinate and a pointer-sequence barrier — late pre-click motion cannot move the pointer backward after the click; relative movement as cumulative/checkpointed representation; drag and touch-emulation transitions obey the same ordering. Tickets: host-issued, tied to lease + view/recovery readiness + geometry + mapping generations, verified against host-clock expiry IMMEDIATELY before OS submission; delayed traffic gets no new lifetime at receipt; timed-out actions reported refused/expired, never silently retried; ordered-sequence gaps are protocol errors or bounded resync, never skipped clicks; duplicates return the retained bounded result within the live epoch; monotonic consumed-sequence floor independent of the result cache (evicted receipts return no-replay/unknown-history, never re-admission); expired press fences queued dependents; release-only cleanup always allowed; periodic held-state reconciliation releases inconsistencies but never synthesizes presses. Text vs keys separated: physical positions/modifiers/repeat ownership distinct from bounded committed Unicode with a qualified injection path — no layout-guess translation, no clipboard smuggling; unavailable text injection surfaced as a limitation with physical keys retained. Focus/geometry/mode/lifecycle checked per batch; cleanup distinguishes requested / OS-submitted / uncertain.

ACCEPTANCE: lab properties (duplicate no-readmit, expiry-before-injection, no resurrection after stall, barrier ordering) against production code; e2e on the real host: type/click/drag through induced stalls and reconnects with per-action disposition logs proving zero stale executions. Provenance: plan sections 7.3, 15.1, 15.2.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for sequence spaces, ticket lifetime/floor logic, and dedupe-cache eviction, independent of the e2e lanes

title: Deterministic property suite: authority, input, recovery, and bounds against production state machines
description:
WHY: The plan's section 24.1 property list is the correctness contract; encoding it as a permanent deterministic suite (not one-off tests) is what lets every later change prove it broke nothing.

SCOPE: On fr-lab, against PRODUCTION state machines: duplicate input identifier cannot admit another click within its live epoch; an old lease never controls a new session; geometry changes reject old coordinate input; obsolete codec configuration never reaches the new decoder; missing references trigger repair or recovery, never indefinite corrupted output; host-clock challenge expiry; ticket expiry immediately before injection; no action resurrection after a stalled reactor; read-only approval enforcement (approval gates thumbnails/audio/clipboard/semantic reads, not just control); controller-handoff serialization; shared-pipeline lifetime (closing one viewer never cancels another's encoder; last unsubscribe stops it); late viewer join waits for a fresh recovery point; old pointer datagrams after a click; client-freshness vs unchanged-screen distinction; committed-vs-uncommitted work in channel cancellation; admitted-vs-irreversibly-submitted OS injection in teardown results. Recovery model rows per the P1_RECOVERY bead. Every failure emits the seed and full event schedule; every bound asserted in BYTES as well as counts.

ACCEPTANCE: suite runs in CI lanes deterministically (two runs, identical logs); a deliberately-broken guard for each property class demonstrates the suite catches it (planted-negative validation); suite documented as the permanent regression gate. Provenance: plan section 24.1.

title: Instrumented input-to-photon latency harness
description:
WHY: The Phase 1 exit gate requires an instrumented latency result, and every future performance claim inherits this harness's honesty rules: distributions and worst useful tails, stages separated, never packet-to-decoder-submission mislabeled as input-to-photon.

SCOPE: An instrumented host application whose input handler changes a known visual target; client-side timestamping of submission and presentation; stage decomposition (input transit, OS/app response, capture wait, conversion, encode, return transit, reassembly/jitter, decode, display wait); local monotonic clocks for stage durations; cross-host offsets only with estimated uncertainty bounds (never raw subtraction of unsynchronized clocks); an optical/high-speed-camera lane documented for later use where practical; output as distributions (p50/p95 and tails) with the measurement scope recorded (process family, direct/relay, cold/warm, refresh rate, capture path). Proposed objectives to measure against, not to claim: direct 2-5 ms RTT p50 <= 45 ms / p95 <= 70 ms; ~40 ms WAN p95 <= 130 ms; warm first useful frame <= 500 ms.

ACCEPTANCE: harness produces reproducible reports on the Phase 1 pair; results recorded with full scope; explicitly labeled as instrumented-workload measurements. Provenance: plan sections 21.1, 21.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Harness self-calibration test: a synthetic known-delay loopback must be measured within stated uncertainty before any real numbers are reported

title: Production loss recovery: fragmentation, repair, recovery generations, startup handshake
description:
WHY: Productionizes the Phase 0 recovery spike. Correctness-critical recovery belongs to Phase 1 — it is explicitly NOT postponable polish, because the Phase 1 exit gate requires surviving real loss.

SCOPE: In fr-transport/fr-media/fr-client: access-unit fragmentation with explicit total length/offset/index/count/stream binding/generations, all arithmetic checked, overlap rejected, duplicates deduplicated without allocation, reassembly bounded in time/metadata/bytes even for hostile tiny fragments; sender cache bounded by bytes and time; receiver missing-range coalescing with clamped ranges/retries/frequency/bytes; separate display vs reference-retention deadlines with the negotiated dependency window (initial ceil(fps x horizon)+2 clamped to 2-12 and byte budget, horizon <= 250 ms provisional); abandon-and-recover when a needed reference exceeds horizon/budget — never feed incomplete pictures to a decoder; startup/reconfiguration handshake exactly as specified (config ack is API-configured, not first-frame; bounded bootstrap IDR retained or refreshed; each milestone with timeout and cleanup; dependent pictures buffered within admitted bounds until IDR decodes; unknown-generation media discarded or held in a tiny pre-config allowance); recovery generations PER SUBSCRIPTION so one viewer's recovery never resets another's decoder; shared-pipeline IDR request coalescing/rate-limiting; chronically failing viewers get an independent operating point or refusal; reliable recovery stream with reset semantics advancing the recovery generation; no per-frame acks in steady state.

ACCEPTANCE: the full lab recovery model (missing first/middle/final fragments, loss before idle, reference repair past display deadline, lost recovery config/ack, exhausted budget, 120 ms repair horizon case, large IDRs, receiver-credit starvation) green against PRODUCTION parsers/state machines with byte-bound assertions and seed-logged failures; real-HEVC e2e under injected loss sustaining useful video. Provenance: plan sections 12.2-12.4, 24.1.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for fragmentation arithmetic (offset/count/overlap/overflow) and sender-cache byte/time eviction

title: Interactive-session agent: consent, indicator, revoke, input lease ownership, watchdog
description:
WHY: The agent runs in the selected user's interactive context and owns everything consent- and input-shaped. Its control path must stay responsive when the encoder is dead, and revoke must never wait on anything slow.

SCOPE: The interactive-session agent role: local approval UI (when enabled, gating any new observation before pixels/thumbnails/audio/clipboard/semantic data), always-visible sharing indicator with immediate revoke (revoke is synchronous at the authority decision point; OS cleanup completion reported separately), input lease ownership with expiry re-checked immediately before EVERY OS submission, key/button held-state tracking for remote injections only, platform permission state surfacing; independent watchdog path so a blocked OS call never holds the lease timer or revoke decision (no authority lock across blocking calls); on OS session change/logout/lock/permission loss, old authority revoked and never inherited; local-input-priority option that suspends the remote lease only where injected-vs-local events are distinguishable (present the limitation honestly where not); approval records device, role, displays, audio scope, session identity; approval expiry on requesting-session end; approval-mode transitions revoke existing grants.

ACCEPTANCE: fault tests — agent alive with dead worker, revoke latency measured and logged, expired lease refuses injection at the submission checkpoint, uncertain release states reported honestly after an input-process crash; UI states screenshot-tested where the platform allows. Provenance: plan sections 5.3, 7.3, 15.2.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): (a) The first platform input-injection adapter lands here: macOS keyboard/pointer injection (CGEvent posting under the Accessibility permission, with the qualified committed-text path distinct from physical-key events), since the session agent owns the submission checkpoint; Windows SendInput and Linux EIS injection land inside their Phase 2 host-adapter beads under the same submission-time checks. (b) The optional OS-supported active-session sleep inhibitor: while a session is actively shared, hold the platform idle-sleep inhibitor (IOKit assertion on macOS, SetThreadExecutionState on Windows, systemd/logind inhibitor on Linux); it prevents idle sleep only — it never defeats lid-close policy or a deliberate local lock, and it releases immediately when the last session ends. Tests: injection refused without Accessibility permission (typed); inhibitor held/released verified in logs across session start/end and crash.

title: fr-core session authority: state machine, leases, challenges, tickets, generations
description:
WHY: This is the heart of "input authority that ends cleanly." Observation permission, media readiness, and input authority are three separate state variables; conflating them is how remote-desktop tools replay stale clicks and leak observation.

SCOPE: In fr-core: the session state machine (Identified -> CapabilitiesChecked -> WaitingApproval? -> ViewOpening -> Viewing -> ControlGranted -> Suspended/Revoke -> Draining -> Closed); a SERIALIZED authority owner (handoff is never a check-then-set race across broker tasks); challenge/renewal on the host's monotonic clock — one-second cadence, three-second provisional renewable deadlines; a response renews only an outstanding unexpired challenge for the current lease (a buffered heartbeat arriving late extends nothing); expired leases are terminal, reacquisition is a new grant re-running approval policy; input-validity tickets as bounded host-side records addressed by opaque random handles (no PKI/custom crypto), lifetime 0.5-1.5 s path-aware, always bounded by the lease, renewed at a cadence comfortably shorter than lifetime without per-action round trips; typed generations (from the F_WORKSPACE bead) fencing every stale artifact; suspend/resume and scheduler-stall as generation boundaries (deadline checked before processing queued work); local approval gating ANY new observation (pixels, thumbnails, audio, clipboard, semantic data) as well as control; the fixed teardown order (revoke input -> release held keys -> invalidate generations -> stop capture admission -> cancel cooperative tasks -> drain bounded sends -> kill stuck worker -> publish closure); pending approvals/reservations with short bounded lifetimes.

ACCEPTANCE: exhaustive unit tests for every transition and every anti-resurrection rule; acknowledgement stages typed as admitted/submitted/observed (never "exactly once"); all tests logged with state-transition traces. Provenance: plan sections 6.3, 7.1-7.3, 15.1.
close_reason: Implemented at f1d89fc: SessionAuthority serialized-owner state machine with observation/readiness/control as separate variables; clock-injected (HostInstant as data, no runtime dep). Covers grant/revoke/handoff serialization, ControllerBusy slot, host-clock challenge renewal with anti-resurrection, ticket lifetimes clamped to lease, authorize_submission pre-OS-submission check, and apply_resume_boundary generation boundary. Design finding fixed: observation drop demotes phase to CapabilitiesChecked so reacquisition is a legal new grant. Gates via rch at this revision: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 26 unit + 2 doc-tests pass. Note: this is the pure-logic core; wiring into the asupersync-owned broker region lands with fr-p1-frd-broker.

title: Client microphone to host: explicit-enable uplink into the qualified virtual-mic endpoint
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes audio bidirectional — talking into a meeting running on the remote workstation is the defining use case. The uplink reuses the downlink's Opus discipline with roles reversed and terminates in the per-OS endpoint proven by the Phase 0 spike.

SCOPE: Client capture (desktop APIs; mobile/browser capture lands with their clients) behind an explicit per-session talk toggle backed by the client OS microphone permission — NEVER activated by connecting, with a visible indicator on both ends; Opus encode at the client; the same sequence/timeline/jitter/generation rules as the downlink; host-side delivery into the qualified virtual-microphone endpoint (PipeWire source on Linux; signed CoreAudio server plugin on macOS; the Windows endpoint per the spike's recommendation — a native non-Rust component with recorded provenance). Where the endpoint is not qualified on a host OS, microphone forwarding is a TYPED UNSUPPORTED capability there — no fake device, no undisclosed driver install. Mic capability is separately advertised and separately approved in approval mode; a viewer never gets it; revoke/lease expiry silences the uplink at the host boundary immediately.

ACCEPTANCE: end-to-end talk test into a real host application per qualified OS with measured added latency; hot-mic security test (activation without explicit enable must fail, logged); lease-expiry silencing verified; endpoint absence produces the typed capability refusal in fr doctor and the client UI. Provenance: plan section 15.4 (v1.4), Phase 0 virtual-mic spike.

title: Host playback audio to client: Opus pipeline, per-OS capture, jitter discipline
description:
WHY: Hearing the remote machine is v1 scope. Audio must never force stale video to display for fake sync, and Windows loopback's cross-session scope must be disclosed, not hidden.

SCOPE: Opus-only downlink: 48 kHz mono/stereo, 10 ms packets nominal; one controlled resample/format boundary from the real device rate; negotiated channels and max packet duration/decoded samples validated before allocation; sequence numbers plus a monotonic sample timeline; explicit capture gaps, silence suppression, device changes, configuration resets. Per-OS sources: ScreenCaptureKit audio on macOS (audio permission/scope distinct from Screen Recording); a selected output monitor via qualified Linux audio APIs; WASAPI render-endpoint loopback on Windows with its endpoint-wide, cross-session scope explicitly disclosed at local setup — authorized as such or left unavailable, never misrepresented as per-app isolation. Client playback: small bounded adaptive jitter buffer with a strict ceiling, packet-loss concealment, slow drift correction anchored to sample timestamps and the client audio clock; bounded A/V offset — fresh video is never held hostage to delayed audio; late packets discarded; device change/reconnect resets the audio generation so stale buffered sound never plays after resume. Playback capture disabled until locally enabled; active only for admitted sessions that request it; approval mode gates it as observation.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e latency/continuity test with induced loss and device switches, logged buffer depths and concealment events; scope-disclosure text verified in setup; lab tests for generation reset and A/V offset bounds. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 23 Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Client-side volume control and instant mute for remote playback audio in every client shell, local-only (no host round trip), state persisted per host

title: Remaining desktop client shells with qualified hardware decode and presentation
description:
WHY: v1 ships native desktop clients on Linux, macOS, and Windows; the first shell exists from Phase 1, and the remaining two reuse fr-client with per-OS decode/presentation qualification.

SCOPE: The two remaining desktop shells per the windowing decision note: window lifecycle, hardware decode to native presentation (D3D swapchain on Windows; the qualified Linux GPU decode + presentation path), full input capture semantics, the standard UI set (machine picker, recent hosts, display selection, toolbar, connection-quality panel, settings, permission explanations), DPI/scale correctness, single-cursor ownership, clean teardown. Client decoders treat host-supplied HEVC as untrusted input to foreign code: the same bounds and containment analysis as host encoders, decode admission against negotiated limits before configuration.

CONSTRAINTS: no GPU-to-CPU readback to fit a UI abstraction; text quality per plan section 14.1 (native pixels when practical, one explicit scaling step, correct color metadata, no accidental limited/full-range mismatch).

ACCEPTANCE: each shell drives a real session against each host OS (the 3x3 pairing smoke-tested, full matrix tracked in the capability table); decode qualification recorded per GPU/driver; e2e scripts with screenshots and logs per platform. Provenance: plan sections 14.1, 16.1, 23 Phase 2.

title: Discovery: local tailnet peers, bounded capability probes, saved hosts, optional directory
description:
WHY: Native clients should find hosts from local Tailscale state without scans; mobile and web cannot read another app's local API, so their baseline is saved hosts and links — and any served directory must be information, never delegated permission.

SCOPE: Desktop: peers from local Tailscale state, then bounded concurrent capability probes ONLY against those node addresses (timeouts/backoff), cached by stable node identity with expiry, invalidated on tailnet change; discovery states distinguished (offline, no interactive session, permission required, ready) where evidence allows; live encode/decode admission revalidated after OS/driver changes. Mobile/web baseline: saved hosts and explicit host links (no bearer tokens in links, ever). Optional authenticated directory served by a known frd: opt-in, restricted by local policy, discovery information only — it must not proxy connections around the viewer's own Tailscale policy or expose inventory contrary to a restricted directory policy; no screenshots, application titles, clipboard previews, or audio in discovery responses; every client device needs its own working tailnet connectivity.

ACCEPTANCE: probe behavior verified bounded (connection counts, backoff) under a flaky-host simulation; directory policy tests (restricted inventory stays restricted); saved-host flow e2e on desktop shells. Provenance: plan section 6.4.

title: Display selection and multi-display: stable catalogs, geometry generations, hotplug
description:
WHY: Multi-monitor desktops are the workstation norm; coordinate-dependent input must be provably bound to the geometry it was aimed at, and display identity is only as stable as the OS actually guarantees.

SCOPE: Display catalog per host: stable local identity within the OS's real guarantees (connector/ID reuse after hotplug handled), pixel bounds, logical bounds, scale, rotation, geometry generation; hotplug/reconfiguration creates a new geometry generation BEFORE coordinate input is accepted; missing/ambiguous mappings refuse rather than guess; only selected displays transmitted, each visible display an independently identified stream under the shared session budget (never one giant bounding-box framebuffer); unobserved displays suspended; the single controller's pointer/keyboard target explicit when viewing several displays; per-display selection UI in the shells; catalog bound to the OS-session/geometry generation.

ACCEPTANCE: lab tests for stale-geometry input rejection; e2e hotplug tests (remove display during a drag, change scale during a click — from the plan's fault list) on each host OS with logs proving refusal rather than misdelivery; multi-display selection round-trips in every desktop shell. Provenance: plan sections 15.5, 24.2.

title: fr doctor / frd status: typed failure explanations and the capability matrix surface
description:
WHY: Explainable failure is a product pillar: permission missing, no supported HEVC decoder, host not in an interactive session, tailnet policy blocked, controller busy, browser transport degraded, mic endpoint unqualified — each a specific, actionable message for humans and stable JSON for agents.

SCOPE: fr doctor --json and frd status --json: Tailscale installation variant and connectivity, HTTPS/certificate state (with renewal countdown), OS permission states per capability (capture/input/clipboard/audio down/audio up/files), hardware encode/decode probe results with cached identity, current sessions and their authority states, sharing scope and approval mode, known-restriction list; every unsupported capability reported as its typed row (passed/failed/blocked/not tested — an untested row is never "supported with caveats"); schema-versioned JSON envelope shared with the robot surface; human output readable without the JSON.

ACCEPTANCE: golden JSON fixtures for representative states; each typed failure reproduced at least once in tests (permission revoked, cert expired, no hardware encoder) with the exact message asserted; doctor output embedded in the diagnostics bundle. Provenance: plan sections 2.1, 18.4, 24.5.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every refusal path emits its typed code to the structured log; golden fixtures cover human AND JSON renderings of identical state

title: Denial-of-service bounds: rate limits, global resource limits, flood fairness
description:
WHY: Plan section 19.3 is an implementation requirement, not only a test list: an admitted peer, a pre-admission stranger, or a flood of metadata must never exhaust the host. The security campaign (Phase 5) attacks these bounds; this bead builds them.

SCOPE: Rate-limit pre-admission connections, expensive codec probes, control requests, cursor-shape uploads, recovery requests, and diagnostic exports; admission accounting for encoder sessions, GPU surfaces, CPU fallback, decoder limits, bandwidth, and per-viewer memory; bounds on message counts AND bytes everywhere (a queue of two access units is still unbounded if access-unit size is); resource limits applied BEFORE a malicious stream can allocate its declared decoded dimensions; global limits for handshake concurrency and duration, pending approvals, half-attached WSS channels, retained request receipts, decoder reconfigurations, and worker restarts; idle-session timeouts that unauthenticated garbage or stale challenges cannot extend; codec probes cancelled when their requesting session disappears (no hardware reservation by mere negotiation); metadata allocations counted (thousands of zero-byte fragments or stream IDs exhaust memory without crossing payload limits); unknown generations, large cursor shapes, long Unicode names, and invalid parameter-set requests rejected before expensive work; revoke/expiry serviced FAIRLY during floods — no high-priority queue is unbounded.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests per limit with planted violations; a lab flood scenario proving revoke latency stays bounded while a peer floods recovery requests, with logged queue/limit counters; limits integrated into the one fr-core limits structure with safe administrator overrides constrained by absolute bounds. Provenance: plan sections 17.2, 19.3.

title: File send/receive over ATP: bounded channel, path safety, atomic publication
description:
WHY: v1.4 promotes file transfer into core scope, reusing asupersync's ATP object-transfer machinery (resumable, integrity-verified) instead of inventing a protocol — the accretive move that turns the remote workstation into a complete workflow.
