SCOPE: Explicit file send/receive between the admitted controlling client and the host on its own bounded channel class within the session: ATP-backed transfer with resumption across reconnects; drag-and-drop initiation where the desktop shells support it plus explicit pick-and-send everywhere; sends land in a locally configured host drop directory; receives come from explicit host-side selection or a configured share directory — the client can never browse or address arbitrary host paths; every received path validated against traversal and symlink escape BEFORE any write; nothing auto-opened or auto-executed; partials written to temporary names and published atomically (cancel/crash never leaves a half-visible file); per-session byte/rate/concurrency budgets admitted separately, transfer traffic sharing congestion capacity without ever sitting ahead of input or starving the freshness contract; progress metadata observable, contents never logged; capability separately advertised and approval-gated; viewers get nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e send/receive of small and multi-GB files with mid-transfer disconnect/resume, logged progress and budgets; path-traversal and symlink-escape attack tests refused with typed errors; a saturation test proving input latency stays bounded during a full-rate transfer. Provenance: plan sections 12.2, 15.6 (v1.4).

title: Linux host adapter: Wayland portal/PipeWire with agent-owned sessions, EIS input, X11 adapter
description:
WHY: Linux hosting spans compositors with genuinely different capability sets; the plan requires per-environment qualification rows and an ownership rule that keeps input authority in the session agent even when capture is delegated.

SCOPE: Wayland: the session agent creates and RETAINS the RemoteDesktop portal session and input connection, passing only the selected PipeWire remote/stream capability to the media worker (a worker must never hold a combined capture+input session); portal sequence with clipboard requested before Start; returned grants, not requested flags, define authorization; restore tokens persisted atomically and rotated (single-use); streams resolved by the strongest identifier (PipeWire serial where available; node IDs are reused) and re-verified after reconnect; compositor-space coordinates vs stream pixels vs crop/scale vs EIS region mapping kept distinct; cursor metadata only when granted; EIS-preferred input path, libei/PipeWire FFI in the platform exception list. X11: explicit adapter using established capture/damage and input mechanisms, its different security assumptions surfaced in diagnostics. systemd user service attaches to the correct graphical session and its D-Bus environment. Qualification rows: GNOME, KDE, and Hyprland/wlroots-family separately (capture, pointer, keyboard, restore, clipboard, playback audio) with exact versions; unsupported rows are actionable refusals or explicit view-only capability — never a privileged input fallback after a portal refusal.

ACCEPTANCE: fault suite green per qualified compositor row with versions recorded; restore-token rotation and node-ID-reuse tests pass; the qualification table published in-repo. Provenance: plan sections 10.1, 23 Phase 2, 24.2.

title: Windows host adapter: Desktop Duplication capture, FFmpeg hardware encode, session-aware service split
description:
WHY: Windows hosting is a v1 requirement; the spike proved the path, this bead productionizes it inside the process-role family with Windows' session model handled honestly.

SCOPE: Desktop Duplication full-display capture with cursor and dirty-region info; prompt frame release with copy-to-owned-GPU-surface when retention would block capture; recreation on documented desktop/display transitions; access-lost / device-removed / resize / rotation / duplication-exhaustion handled explicitly; capture device qualified against the actual display adapter (hybrid GPUs); qualified SDR conversion/tone-mapping without changing user display settings (DuplicateOutput1 format behavior); FFmpeg hardware encode (NVENC/AMF/QSV per probe) in the media worker. Service split: the service never captures Session 0 as the user's desktop; the interactive agent binds to the intended session with its executable, launch permissions, and named-pipe endpoints session-bound; lock screens, user changes, and secure-desktop transitions are typed capability changes; SendInput integrity-level limits surfaced as capability rows (no promise of elevated-window or secure-desktop control); protected-content blackouts and integrity-restricted input reported separately from transport failure; mixed-DPI monitors with negative virtual-desktop coordinates and rotation mapped correctly.

ACCEPTANCE: the common Phase 2 session/input fault suite green on real Windows hardware with device evidence; capture-transition tests (lock/unlock, resolution change, GPU reset) logged; input refusal on elevated windows verified and reported as the typed limitation. Provenance: plan sections 8.3, 10.3, 23 Phase 2.

title: Service lifecycle and installers: idempotent registration, permission setup, honest uninstall
description:
WHY: Installation is where consent is established and where trust is most often burned. The installer must detect reality (Tailscale variant, permissions, certificates, conflicts, hardware) before advertising a working host, and uninstall must remove FrankenRemote without touching the user's Tailscale.

SCOPE: Per-OS installers/service registration (launchd family on macOS with signing/notarization; Windows service + interactive agent; systemd user/system units on Linux attached to the right graphical session): idempotent registration; setup flow that verifies tailnet connectivity, obtains OS permissions through signed user-visible paths (a headless service cannot complete consent), checks hardware encode support, provisions certificates, records sharing-scope and audio/file consent locally; only narrowly required firewall rules for the tailnet service; never enabling a public/LAN listener after failure; repair preserves consent without broadening it; uninstall removes services and files, leaves Tailscale and tailnet policy untouched; offline installation of packaged assets supported (cert issuance and Tailscale enrollment still need their own connectivity).

ACCEPTANCE: install/repair/uninstall cycles tested per OS with permission-state assertions before and after; packaging smoke tests (the Phase 2 exit requirement) green; failure-mode tests (no Tailscale, permission denied, port conflict) produce the typed setup guidance. Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 23 Phase 2.

title: Shared clipboard: default-on bidirectional text sync with bounded transfers and echo prevention
description:
WHY: v1.4 declares the shared clipboard table stakes: copy on either side, paste on the other, automatically — while keeping the privacy and bounds discipline that stops it becoming a covert channel or a parser exploit.

SCOPE: Automatic bidirectional text clipboard synchronization between the controlling client and the host, DEFAULT-ON for the controlling session, visible off switch on both ends; one MiB validated UTF-8 per item (configurable), carried on its own bounded chunked channel with declared total length and chunk sequence — never smuggled through the 64 KiB control parser; sequence identifiers and source labels preventing echo loops; controller-only (read-only viewers get nothing); approval mode covers clipboard as observation; Linux portal clipboard requested before session Start and honored only per the returned grant; clipboard can be absent even where input works — typed capability row; reject invalid encodings and cancellation-sensitive partial transfers before publishing to the OS; session buffers cleared on closure (without promising to erase OS clipboard-manager history or overwrite newer local values); clipboard content NEVER in logs, error messages, URLs, or traces; image clipboard as a negotiated optional capability over the file-transfer channel (deferred follow-on, not this bead's blocker).

ACCEPTANCE: e2e copy/paste both directions on all three host OSes; echo-loop lab test; oversized/invalid-encoding refusal tests; a log-scrubbing test proving clipboard bytes never appear in diagnostics. Provenance: plan section 15.3 (v1.4), 10.1.

title: Bounded viewer admission and controller handoff over shared pipelines
description:
WHY: The initial viewer limit is deliberately small — one controller plus two read-only viewers subject to resource admission — and shared-pipeline ownership is where multi-viewer systems usually corrupt authority or leak resources. Added only after single-controller behavior is correct.

SCOPE: Viewer admission against encoder sessions, GPU surfaces, bandwidth, and per-viewer memory; shared encoded streams only where codec configuration, viewport, and operating point match, extra encoder sessions through admission otherwise; shared pipelines owned by the OS share session region — closing one viewer never cancels another's encoder, last unsubscribe stops the pipeline, a failed shared pipeline suspends affected control/readiness while unrelated display pipelines continue; slow read-only viewers degraded or disconnected independently, never backpressuring the controller; controller handoff serialized in the authority owner — second requests observe, wait, or request handoff; handoff invalidates the old lease and releases its held state before admitting the new controller; a new controller is denied or explicitly handed off, never auto-substituted by arrival order; read-only viewers cannot move the host cursor, change the controller's viewport, use the clipboard, or force global quality changes; per-viewer counters (pipelines, encoder sessions, surfaces, cached bytes, queued repair).

ACCEPTANCE: lab properties for shared-pipeline lifetime and handoff serialization (kill first viewer of a shared encoder, disconnect a slow secondary, join a third during recovery — the plan's fault list); e2e three-viewer session with per-viewer budget logs. Provenance: plan sections 2.2, 7.1, 15.5, 24.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests for admission arithmetic (sessions, surfaces, per-viewer bytes) with planted over-budget cases
- [ ] Host-side connected-sessions list in the session agent UI: device name, role, capabilities in use (view/control/audio/clipboard/files), with per-session revoke — not just the aggregate indicator

title: Media-worker OS sandboxing and privilege reduction per platform
description:
WHY: A separate worker process gives crash/hang isolation by itself — NOT a security sandbox. Client decoders and host encoders both run foreign code on untrusted input, so the plan requires OS-supported containment compatible with GPU/capture access, and explicit documentation of residual trust where real enforcement is impossible. Claiming isolation that is not enforced is forbidden.

SCOPE: Per platform, apply and TEST the strongest sandbox compatible with the worker's GPU/capture needs: Windows — restricted tokens, job objects, reduced integrity, restricted inherited handles; macOS — sandbox profiles/entitlement minimization for the signed worker; Linux — namespaces, seccomp filters, and landlock where GPU access permits. Document the actual enforced restrictions on filesystem, IPC, network, process creation, and input APIs per OS, and record residual trust explicitly where an adapter cannot be meaningfully sandboxed (a compromised same-user unsandboxed worker is never claimed harmless). Workers continue to receive no Tailscale control socket, certificate keys, approval endpoint, or input-lease capability (enforced by the broker's role-capability IPC). Client decode workers get the same treatment: host-supplied HEVC is untrusted input to foreign code even on a trusted tailnet.

ACCEPTANCE: per-OS sandbox capability table (enforced / partial / not enforceable, with reasons) committed; escape-attempt tests for each enforced restriction (open a network socket, read outside allowed paths, reach the approval IPC — all must fail with logs); the shipped boundary tested as shipped, not as designed; residual-trust statements mirrored into SECURITY.md. Provenance: plan sections 5.4, 19.1, 19.2.

title: Android app: native Kotlin/Jetpack Compose application over the shared core
description:
WHY: The Android counterpart to the iOS bead: first-class Kotlin/Jetpack Compose UI in mobile/android, same shared core, same authority discipline, with Android's own media and lifecycle rules respected.

SCOPE: Compose app: machine picker/saved hosts/links, session viewer decoding to a Surface via MediaCodec (never copying decoded pixels through Rust memory), trackpad and direct-touch modes, keyboard including hardware keyboards and IME committed-text semantics (composition local until committed; cancelled on session replacement), pan/zoom with the defined transforms, talk toggle with Android mic permission, file send/receive via SAF within scoped-storage limits, settings/quality panel/permission explanations; lifecycle: background releases control, resume = fresh lease + recovery point, rotation requires current mapping, network transitions re-evaluate the route and never carry stale authority; predictive back, edge-to-edge, dark theme, TalkBack labels; signing per platform mechanism. Media APIs remain foreign trust boundaries even behind safe-looking wrappers — decode admission against negotiated limits before configuration.

ACCEPTANCE: real-device session against each host OS; background/resume and rotation authority tests green; thermal steady-state decode measured; e2e scripts with logcat capture; UI review against platform conventions. Provenance: plan sections 14.4, 16.2 (v1.4), 23 Phase 3.

title: Browser audio: Opus playback path and getUserMedia microphone uplink
description:
WHY: Browser clients need both directions too: play the host's audio, and speak into the host's virtual mic — within the browser's gesture, permission, and worklet constraints.

SCOPE: Downlink: probe an actual supported Opus decode/output path; the fallback is a small WASM Opus decoder feeding an AudioWorklet with bounded preallocated work, no network fetches or blocking calls in the worklet; bounded ring/credit protocol with transferable buffers as baseline (SharedArrayBuffer only as an optional optimization with its cross-origin-isolation requirements stated, never an unmentioned prerequisite); audio starts on a browser-permitted user gesture and stops on lifecycle transitions; measure worklet/buffer overhead on phones before claiming low added latency. Uplink: getUserMedia capture behind the same explicit talk toggle, browser permission prompt respected, Opus encode within the bounded WASM budget, the standard uplink sequence/generation rules, indicator visible.

ACCEPTANCE: Chrome and Safari playback + talk e2e against a real host; hidden-tab and gesture-requirement behavior verified; buffer-depth and added-latency measurements recorded per browser. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 16.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] wasm-bindgen unit tests for the ring/credit protocol; worklet underrun/overrun events logged with counters

title: Browser qualification matrix: Chrome and Safari rows with decode-path evidence
description:
WHY: The v1.3 bar makes current Chrome and Safari the qualification target; this bead produces the evidence-backed matrix that says exactly which browser/OS/hardware combinations are supported, degraded (WSS), or unsupported — 'WebCodecs exists' is not an acceptance test.

SCOPE: For each combination (Chrome on Windows/macOS/Linux-with-hw-caveats; Safari on macOS/iOS-adjacent): exact browser version, OS build, codec probe output, transport mode achieved (WebTransport vs WSS), decode-path evidence (hardware vs software), presentation behavior including the idle/first-frame/last-frame/low-cadence cases, input capability rows (keyboard lock, pointer lock, clipboard, fullscreen), audio both ways, file-transfer capability; each row passed/failed/blocked/not tested; the published matrix distinguishes supported, degraded, and unsupported and feeds fr doctor and the README known-restrictions list.

ACCEPTANCE: the matrix committed with retained probe outputs per row; unsupported combinations produce the typed in-product explanation; matrix wired into the release-evidence flow. Provenance: plan sections 16.3, 24.4, v1.3 note.

title: Browser origin security: exact-Origin checks, nonce bootstrap, ticket attachment, CSP
description:
WHY: Tailscale authenticates the connecting NODE, not the web origin running on it. A hostile page on an admitted machine must gain nothing. This is release-blocking security, not browser polish.

SCOPE: Serve the UI only from the configured host HTTPS origin; validate configured Host/authority (and SNI where exposed); require the EXACT expected Origin for all state-changing requests and WebSocket/WebTransport establishment; deny wildcard CORS, null origins, cross-origin fetches, and state changes via GET (a navigation GET serves only static content — never a ticket, lease, or capture start); Fetch Metadata as defense in depth, never the sole test; short-lived one-use nonce via origin-checked same-origin HTTPS POST, bound to verified peer + requested session/role, required before any sensitive operation; non-executable JSON with no-store/nosniff (no JSONP, no nonce-bearing scripts); since browser sockets cannot carry custom handshake headers, authenticate the application session in a bounded FIRST reliable message after the origin-checked transport opens — until then no pixels, audio, input, codec work, or directory expansion; every auxiliary channel attaches with a role-specific one-use ticket (a bare session ID attaches nothing); nonces/tickets never in query strings, links, logs, or referrers; unauthenticated handshakes rate-limited, unused tickets expired; restrictive CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', safe referrer policy, no-store on sensitive responses; browser state invalidated on session closure; native WSS clients follow the same origin/nonce contract — missing Origin is not an alternate authentication mode.

ACCEPTANCE: attack tests from the plan's list — malicious iframes, DNS rebinding/Host tricks, cross-origin WebSockets, stale/replayed tickets, bfcache restoration, request smuggling/header ambiguity in the selected HTTP stack — all refused with typed logs; CSP verified by automated header assertions. Provenance: plan sections 16.4, 24.3.

title: File transfer on mobile and browser within platform file-access limits
description:
WHY: File send/receive is core scope; mobile and browser platforms constrain file access (document pickers, SAF, browser download/upload sandboxes), so the capability ships within those limits with honest capability rows rather than pretending desktop semantics.

SCOPE: iOS: send via share sheet/document picker, receive into the app's Documents with export via share sheet. Android: SAF-based pick/send and receive with scoped storage. Browser: upload via file input/drag-drop; receive as browser-mediated download (the viewer sandbox rules mean downloads are user-gesture-bound; label what is and is not possible per browser). All platforms reuse the ATP channel, budgets, atomic publication, and path-safety rules from the desktop bead; capability rows per platform recorded (e.g., folder sync explicitly desktop-only in v1); progress UI in each client.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e send/receive per platform with disconnect/resume where the platform permits; capability rows in the matrix; refusal paths (unsupported direction on a platform) typed and user-legible. Provenance: plan section 15.6 (v1.4), 16.2, 16.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for each platform file-adapter layer; e2e transfer logs capture per-chunk progress and refusal codes

title: iOS app: native SwiftUI application over the shared core
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes the iOS client a first-class native SwiftUI application — platform-conventional, polished, in this monorepo under mobile/ios — not a thin wrapper around a Rust view.

SCOPE: SwiftUI app: machine picker (saved hosts + host links; no bearer tokens in links), session viewer with VideoToolbox decode output to native display layers/Metal (never the UI toolkit's image path), trackpad mode and direct-touch mode with visibly different semantics, long press/secondary click/scroll/modifier keys/explicit text entry discoverable, software+hardware keyboard support with IME composition as local state committed explicitly (cancelled on view/session replacement, never replayed into a different desktop), pan/zoom with the defined coordinate transform (local zoom = client transform; host crop = acknowledged mapping generation), the talk toggle with iOS mic permission, file send/receive within iOS file-access limits (share sheet / document picker), settings, connection-quality panel, permission explanations; lifecycle: backgrounding releases control, resume obtains a fresh lease and recovery frame (never replaying queued taps), orientation changes require a current client mapping, network transitions (Wi-Fi/cellular) re-evaluate the VPN route — migration never overrides changed peer identity or expired authority; safe areas, dynamic type, dark mode, accessibility labels; signing/entitlements per platform mechanism.

ACCEPTANCE: real-device session against each host OS; background/resume authority tests green (the Phase 3 exit requirement); UI review against platform conventions; e2e scripts with device logs; thermal steady-state decode measured (a cool-phone burst is not the envelope). Provenance: plan sections 14.4, 16.2 (v1.4), 23 Phase 3.

title: Mobile FFI boundary: Swift package and Kotlin/JNI bindings over fr-client
description:
WHY: v1.4 commits both mobile apps to first-class native UIs over the shared Rust core through ONE narrow audited boundary per platform — all logic stays in Rust; the bindings move calls, callbacks, and buffers, nothing more.

SCOPE: Per the mobile-FFI decision note: a C-ABI surface over fr-client (session lifecycle, host connection, display/viewport state, input submission, capability/diagnostic queries, media handles for platform decode paths, audio uplink control, file-transfer operations) with lifecycle-safe handle semantics (no use-after-free reachable from Swift/Kotlin misuse — handles generation-checked at the boundary); a Swift package wrapping it idiomatically (async/await bridging to the Rust core's completion model, Sendable-correct types); a Kotlin/JNI wrapper equally idiomatic (coroutines bridging, no leaked global refs); build integration in-monorepo — repository-owned commands build the Rust core for iOS (aarch64-apple-ios) and Android (aarch64/armv7 as decided) targets and package the XCFramework/AAR; the boundary is audited like fr-ffi: documented ownership, callback threading, and shutdown order.

CONSTRAINTS: no product logic in bindings; decoded video never routed through the FFI as CPU pixels — media handles hand off to VideoToolbox/MediaCodec platform paths.

ACCEPTANCE: binding unit tests on both platforms (including deliberate misuse: double-free, stale handle, callback after shutdown — all safely refused); a headless smoke connecting to a real host from an iOS simulator/Android emulator where transport permits, else on-device; CI lane building both packages from the monorepo. Provenance: plan section 16.2 (v1.4), P0 decision notes.

title: Mobile qualification: thermal, lifecycle, rotation, and network-transition evidence
description:
WHY: Phones fail differently: thermal throttling, aggressive background suspension, IME complexity, and route flapping. The Phase 3 exit gate needs device evidence that none of these can preserve stale control or misrepresent the decode envelope.

SCOPE: On representative iOS and Android hardware (recorded models/OS builds): sustained-decode thermal equilibrium (not cool-phone bursts) at the negotiated operating points; background/foreground cycling under memory pressure with authority assertions after every resume; rotation during active control; Wi-Fi-to-cellular and cellular-to-Wi-Fi transitions mid-session (route re-evaluation, identity revalidation, no stale-authority carryover — mobile suspension may prevent clean client teardown, which is exactly why host lease expiry is mandatory: verify it fires); IME composition cancelled across reconnects; hardware-keyboard rows; audio both ways on-device; capability matrix rows filled per device.

ACCEPTANCE: the mobile rows of the capability matrix with retained measurements; every lifecycle test logged with host-side authority traces proving expiry did its job. Provenance: plan sections 16.2, 23 Phase 3, 24.2.

title: fr-web: WASM state machine, JS boundary, WebCodecs pipeline, self-hosted assets
description:
WHY: The browser client runs the SAME Rust core compiled to WASM, with a deliberately narrow JavaScript boundary for what only the browser can do — transport handles, WebCodecs, presentation, DOM input, audio nodes. Chrome and Safari are the qualification bar (v1.3).

SCOPE: fr-web WASM entrypoint over fr-client; JS boundary modules for WebTransport (and WSS), VideoDecoder configuration from exact negotiated hvcC with complete access units (one EncodedVideoChunk per admitted AU, correct key/delta designation, timestamps in API units; in-band parameter-set changes rejected until renegotiation), presentation to a browser surface, keyboard/pointer/pointer-lock/fullscreen capture with browser-reserved-shortcut capability rows, lifecycle handling (pagehide, bfcache restoration, hidden-tab throttling, decoder reclamation, worker failure) each triggering a fresh usable-view check before control resumes — hidden tabs never preserve input authority; VideoFrame objects closed promptly with bounded decode queue AND renderer retention, worker-based decode where supported, no per-frame flush; asset serving from frd — self-hosted, no CDN, no third-party scripts/fonts/analytics, bounded sizes, version handshake so a stale cached client renegotiates or reloads without replaying input; no service-worker authority; the browser build inherits zero desktop FFI (feature-graph enforced).

ACCEPTANCE: real Chrome session against a real host end to end; lifecycle tests (tab hide, bfcache, decoder reset) proving authority never survives staleness, with browser-console and host logs captured; asset-version skew test. Provenance: plan sections 16.3, 23 Phase 3.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): the browser client's user interface itself — machine entry (saved hosts and host links; no local-API enumeration in a browser), session viewer chrome, input toolbar and mode controls, the talk toggle, connection-quality panel, permission/capability explanations (including the typed unsupported-combination message from the probe), and settings — kept deliberately small, self-hosted, dependency-free, and consistent with the desktop shells' information architecture. UI tests: capability-refusal rendering, stale-asset version-handshake reload, and keyboard-capture indicator states, driven through the e2e harness with browser console + host logs captured.

title: WSS compatibility profile: bound channels, receiver credit, honest degradation labeling
description:
WHY: WSS is the explicit degraded fallback for browsers without qualified WebTransport (expected: some Safari versions) and for native clients behind hostile networks. It must keep every authorization and expiry semantic while being honest that TCP head-of-line exists.

SCOPE: Separately bound control, video, and audio WSS channels, each attached to the admitted peer/session via role-specific one-use capabilities; a media replacement never implicitly acquires a fresh controller; if the implementation multiplexes over one TCP connection, the shared-transport limitation is labeled; bounded application send queues PLUS receiver-granted outstanding-byte/frame credit for media (bufferedAmount is outbound-only; browser WS has no receive backpressure — the host never sends merely because its socket accepts bytes); credits returned only when the application frees receive budget; receipt/decode/presentation acks distinguishable; stale-channel replacement fences the old generation immediately, stops writing, closes from the capable endpoint, ignores late old-generation data; bounded concurrent closing channels with backoff so resets cannot become their own attack; input lease retention governed by view freshness, never socket-open state; compression disabled for media and sensitive control; clipboard stays off the input channel; the profile is labeled degraded in diagnostics and never presented as datagram-equivalent.

ACCEPTANCE: credit-starvation and channel-replacement lab tests; an e2e browser session forced onto WSS with measured behavior recorded separately from native-datagram results; downgrade attempts that would remove security checks rejected. Provenance: plan sections 12.5, 17.3.

title: Controller tuning: Auto/Text/Motion policies and operating-point management
description:
WHY: Phase 4 turns the deterministic v0 controller into workstation-grade adaptation: document work keeps its pixel grid, motion work trades detail for smoothness, and the user sees three choices, not a page of vendor switches.

SCOPE: Text policy (reduce unnecessary frame rate first, preserve spatial resolution), Motion policy (trade spatial detail for presentation smoothness), Auto selection between them from damage/motion statistics; expert override kept off the main UI; operating-point ladders per codec backend with admission-checked transitions (a new-encoder change admitted against temporary overlap budgets or via explicit stop/restart — seamless replacement is not free); per-host/per-path aggregate ceilings so three adapting sessions cannot each claim full capacity; frame-rate reduction accounting for per-picture serialization cost (fewer frames at the same bitrate means bigger pictures); bounded probe bursts for upward moves; relay-vs-direct path transitions resetting estimates.

ACCEPTANCE: scenario matrix runs (text editing, terminal scrolling, video motion, mixed) showing stable operating points without oscillation, logged decision traces replayable; readable-text metrics at the constrained operating points recorded; user-facing mode switch e2e in the shells. Provenance: plan sections 3.2, 13.3, 23 Phase 4.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for hysteresis/dwell/ladder-transition functions as pure logged-input functions

title: Measured copy and queue optimization pass
description:
WHY: Zero-copy is a measured property per qualified path, not a slogan. Before advanced codec tools, the plan requires optimizing observed copies and queues — the cheapest real latency wins.

SCOPE: Instrument and enumerate every copy on each qualified path (capture->convert->encode host-side; receive->decode->present client-side); eliminate or justify each (a slower-named encoder that avoids an expensive transfer may win); verify surface-ownership discipline survives the optimizations (borrowed buffers still released at documented points, padding still cleared); re-measure stage latencies and update the per-path copy counts reported in diagnostics; queue-limit re-tuning from soak high-water marks.

ACCEPTANCE: before/after copy counts and stage latencies per path with retained runs; no ownership regression (sanitizer/assert lanes still green); diagnostics reporting the real counts. Provenance: plan sections 11.1, 21.3, 23 Phase 4.

title: Cursor separation polish and damage-aware scheduling
description:
WHY: Cursor movement must never force full-screen encodes, and prediction must reconcile with remote reality without double cursors or divergent clicks.

SCOPE: Cursor shape as reliable state (identity, hotspot, scale, visibility, bounds; unknown-shape safe fallback), position as replaceable datagram state; single rendering owner negotiated by capability bit (no second cursor where capture composites it); local prediction hidden/reconciled when the remote OS confines, warps, or suppresses the pointer; relative/pointer-lock and touch-emulation modes each with one cursor owner and coherent click coordinates; damage-aware capture/encode scheduling that skips redundant work when only the cursor moved.

ACCEPTANCE: cursor-only-motion test showing no full-frame encodes; pointer-lock and warp reconciliation e2e; visual double-cursor check across shells and browsers; scheduling decisions logged. Provenance: plan sections 3.2, 11.4.

title: Diagnostic bundle, sanitized traces, and deterministic controller replay
description:
WHY: Explainable performance is a product pillar: a bounded ring buffer, an exportable sanitized bundle, and deterministic replay of adaptation decisions in the lab — without ever recording the screen by default.

SCOPE: Bounded ring buffer of session events (versions, hardware capabilities, negotiated settings, connection path, stage timings, queue high-water marks, drops, recovery events, controller decisions with input snapshots); on-demand file export — no database, no remote telemetry; sanitization covering host/user names, paths, window titles, addresses, certificate identifiers, and library error strings (reviewed before export), with codec payloads, TLS keys, session nonces, input text, and clipboard/file contents excluded ALWAYS; bounded trace bytes and event rates; replay harness feeding sanitized traces into fr-lab reproducing recorded policy/state transitions (replay reproduces decisions, not GPU drivers — labeled as such); the why-is-this-slow surface in clients naming the actual bottleneck (relay path, encoder overload, copies, decoder backlog, refresh mismatch, thermal, queue growth).

ACCEPTANCE: export/sanitize round-trip tests with planted sensitive strings proving scrubbing; a captured real-session trace replays deterministically twice with identical decision logs; the diagnosis surface verified against induced bottlenecks. Provenance: plan sections 3.4, 18.4, 23 Phase 4.

title: ATP folder-synchronization jobs with explicit conflict policy
description:
WHY: v1.4's file capability completes with standing folder-sync jobs on the proven transfer channel — the remote workstation keeps working directories aligned without a third-party tool.

SCOPE: Locally configured host-side job definitions (explicit local directories, one-way or bidirectional, per-client opt-in acceptance); ATP resumption across reconnects; the explicit conflict policy — keep both with a conflict marker, never silent overwrite; change detection within the job directories with bounded scan cost; job state observable (per-file progress, last-sync, conflicts) in doctor/diagnostics; budgets shared with the transfer channel (never ahead of input, never starving freshness); path-safety rules identical to the transfer bead; jobs pause under approval revocation or session end and resume cleanly.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e bidirectional sync with concurrent edits producing conflict copies (no silent loss — verified by content hash); disconnect mid-sync resumes without corruption; a large-tree soak with logged budgets; desktop-only capability row recorded (mobile/browser sync explicitly out for v1). Provenance: plan section 15.6 (v1.4), 23 Phase 4.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for conflict-resolution decisions and bounded scan cost; sync-job event log per file with content hashes

title: Idle discipline and settle-to-sharp refinement
description:
WHY: Static desktops should cost almost nothing, and when motion stops the user deserves a sharper picture — an HEVC re-encode of the verified current capture, not a PNG backchannel and not a queued pre-scroll frame.

SCOPE: Idle: stationary screens stop video transmission except genuine refresh/refinement; periodic source-verification metadata distinguishes idle from a hung pipeline (bounded verification captures at a declared cadence where cheap evidence is unavailable, with cost reported); first damage exits idle promptly — measure the first-changed-frame-after-long-idle path explicitly; the final refinement before idle proven to actually present (some codec/browser paths retain output when no more frames arrive — the adapter must prove prompt output at low cadence or use a bounded, measured flush-and-IDR policy with its cost reported; never endless dummy video). Settle-to-sharp: after motion settles, a higher-quality encode of a NEWLY verified capture within available budget; rate-limited settle detection; recovery headroom reserved so refinement never starves interactive damage; honest labeling — refinement improves quantization, it cannot restore 4:2:0 chroma.

ACCEPTANCE: static-screen soak showing near-zero encode work with freshness evidence continuing; measured refinement latency and quality delta on text content; idle-exit latency measured; all logged. Provenance: plan sections 13.4, 14.1, 23 Phase 4.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit/lab tests for settle-detection rate limiting, idle-exit triggering, and refinement-vs-damage priority

title: Recovery tuning across the network impairment matrix
description:
WHY: The recovery machinery is correct from Phase 1; Phase 4 proves and tunes it across the full impairment envelope so the constrained-network operating point can be honestly advertised (or honestly refused).

SCOPE: Run and tune against: healthy direct, ~40 ms RTT, ~120 ms RTT with 5 Mbps and 1% loss, random loss, burst loss, variable jitter, abrupt capacity reduction, forced DERP relay, bandwidth step changes immediately after idle, direct-to-relay transition during a drag; impairment injected at labeled points (inner datagrams vs outer tunnel packets vs TCP/DERP stalls are not interchangeable — record which); sweep burst loss and recovery-frame size; measure stall frequency/duration, recovery bytes, time-with-input-suspended, and text readability at each point; tune repair budgets, horizons, and controller interaction; the 720p/1080p readable-document target at the constrained point gets a support claim ONLY if bounded stalls and useful text are demonstrated.

ACCEPTANCE: a results table per impairment row with retained runs; updated default budgets with rationale; any unreachable operating point documented as such in the capability matrix rather than shipped as a claim. Provenance: plan sections 12.2, 21.1, 24.4.

title: Hardware and network comparison matrix including the Sunshine/Moonlight baseline
description:
WHY: The performance story must survive an honest comparison: same displays, refresh rates, content, impairment, bitrate accounting, and capture method as a well-configured Sunshine/Moonlight pair — plus native platform tools where applicable. A low-latency number achieved by quietly lowering resolution is not equivalent quality.

SCOPE: The hardware matrix (Apple Silicon; representative NVIDIA/AMD/Intel; low-power mobile decoders) with exact GPU/driver/OS/encoder/decoder/pixel-format/settings recorded per row; the network matrix from the impairment bead re-run on release candidates; input-to-photon distributions from the instrumented harness with the optical lane where practical; equal-conditions Sunshine/Moonlight comparison including text-readability, scale correctness, cursor alignment, and color-range behavior — not only aggregate video metrics; recordings/screenshots only in the explicitly authorized benchmark lane; Tailscale's own overhead reported separately (neither charged nor hidden); WSS profile measured independently under its own assumptions.

ACCEPTANCE: the comparison report with retained raw runs, every number carrying its measurement scope; no claim published that outruns a retained artifact; support rows updated from results. Provenance: plan sections 21.1-21.3, 24.4.

title: Long-duration and thermal-equilibrium qualification
description:
WHY: Short benchmarks lie: encoders throttle, queues creep, and daemons leak only over hours. Release claims require sustained-use evidence at thermal equilibrium on both hosts and clients.

SCOPE: Multi-hour continuous sessions per qualified host/client pair at representative operating points: RSS/CPU/GPU-memory tracked for the whole process family (idle broker envelope re-verified after teardown: under 25 MiB / under 0.1% core targets, GPU allocations counted separately from CPU RSS); queue high-water marks flat; thermal throttling behavior observed and reported (host encode and mobile decode); certificate renewal occurring mid-session handled cleanly; multi-day idle daemon soak with zero growth; sleep/wake cycles across the soak.

ACCEPTANCE: soak reports per pair with retained metric series; any drift/leak fixed and re-run; results feed the published operating envelopes with their measurement scopes stated. Provenance: plan sections 21.1, 21.3, 23 Phase 5.

title: PROTOCOL.md v1 freeze: golden messages and an interoperable test peer across all profiles
description:
WHY: Version 1 of the wire contract freezes only with proof that the spec, the implementation, and an independent peer agree — a self-round-tripping encoder/parser pair proves nothing.

SCOPE: Reconcile PROTOCOL.md against the implemented reality (every divergence resolved deliberately, not documented around); golden message fixtures covering every message class on every transport profile (native QUIC, WebTransport, WSS); an interoperable test peer exercising the goldens against the production endpoints; version-negotiation and downgrade-rejection tests (a WSS fallback retains authorization, bounds, and input-expiry semantics; profiles that would remove required checks are refused); the declared compatibility window documented; robot-schema and capability-name versions pinned separately.

ACCEPTANCE: the frozen v1 document, goldens in-tree, peer runs green in CI lanes against all profiles; a compatibility-window test with a deliberately older peer negotiating or refusing cleanly. Provenance: plan sections 17.1, 17.3.

title: Adversarial security campaign: fuzzing, identity attacks, hostile media, origin attacks
description:
WHY: The plan's section 24.3 list is the pre-release adversarial contract. Every row is a requirement to execute with retained evidence — none may be marked done from inspection.

SCOPE: Fuzz the wire parser, HEVC configuration normalization (VPS/SPS/PPS validation against the admitted subset), geometry arithmetic, input decoder, and local IPC framing, with coverage-guided harnesses seeded from goldens; independent decoder interoperability tests for generated streams. Identity attacks: unrelated LAN source, forged 100.x on the wrong interface, external sharee, shared-in node, subnet-routed source, out-of-scope same-tailnet user under the own-user default, malicious web origin on an admitted client. Protocol/session attacks: forged Serve headers, unauthorized local IPC approval, stale-generation worker messages, oversized media configuration, excessive fragment counts, duplicate-fragment memory inflation, recovery-request floods, clipboard echo loops, file-transfer path traversal and symlink escape, transfer-budget floods, microphone activation without explicit enable, replayed attachment tickets, 0-RTT application operations, alternate-address migration, pre-admission media, origin-less WSS bypass. TLS: invalid/expired certificates, wrong hostname/ALPN, tampered QUIC packets. Hostile media: valid-looking HEVC parameter sets with excessive DPB demands, in-band configuration changes inside ordinary media, audio packets declaring excessive decoded duration. Update-system attacks live in the updates bead; DLL/library search-path injection and mixed helper generations tested here too. Approval-mode bypass attempts against thumbnails/audio/clipboard/semantic reads.

ACCEPTANCE: every row passed/failed/blocked with retained artifacts and logs; failures fixed and re-run; fuzzers left running in a scheduled lane with crash triage documented. Provenance: plan sections 19.2, 19.3, 24.3.

title: Publish the supported matrix and known restrictions (README + fr doctor)
description:
WHY: Release honesty is a deliverable: one compact capability/result matrix, rows strictly passed/failed/blocked/not-tested, restrictions legible to users and agents — no evidence bureaucracy, no untested row dressed as supported-with-caveats.

SCOPE: Compile the release matrix from the retained evidence: host OS rows (capture/input/clipboard/audio-down/audio-up/files per compositor and OS version), client rows (desktop/iOS/Android/Chrome/Safari with decode-path evidence), transport rows (native QUIC, WebTransport, WSS-degraded), operating-point rows from the benchmark bead; the known-restrictions list in README and fr doctor (elevated windows on Windows, Wayland compositor gaps, Safari transport status, mic-endpoint status per OS, mobile file limits, etc.); the README trued up from spec-tense to shipped reality where phases landed; every public quantitative claim machine-derived or artifact-linked.

ACCEPTANCE: matrix published; doctor serves the same rows; a cross-check script verifies README claims against the matrix rows so the two cannot drift. Provenance: plan sections 24.5, 26.

title: Update system: staged signed generations, atomic activation, verified rollback
description:
WHY: An ABI-coupled process family (broker/agent/worker + native media libraries) must update as one generation or not at all; a half-updated family is a correctness and security failure.

SCOPE: Stage a complete signed generation, validate it, activate atomically; never replace one helper alone; default deferred activation until idle, explicit immediate activation ending sessions cleanly first; rollback generation preserved with an installation receipt; post-activation validation that permissions, helper identity, native libraries, and local IPC still work (version strings prove nothing); publisher/signature verification anchored by the platform mechanism, unsigned/unexpected-role artifacts rejected; update metadata cannot force a silent rollback to a vulnerable build — explicit local rollback uses a previously verified package under local authority; capped download/extraction sizes and archive-path validation before privileged writes; resume-after-partial-failure activates a complete verified generation or retains the previous one — no mixed helper/FFmpeg ABI family ever.

ACCEPTANCE: update/rollback/partial-failure/downgrade-attack tests per OS with retained logs; a deliberately corrupted staged generation refused; the receipt format documented. Provenance: plan section 20.4, 24.3.

title: Phase 0 exit gate: all architectural-risk spikes resolved with evidence
description:
WHY: Phase 0 exists so the risks that could invalidate the architecture die first, in small real vertical experiments — before the product is built around assumptions. This epic closes only when every spike row has evidence.

EXIT CRITERIA: every Phase 0 bead resolved with a reproducible command, exact hardware/software identity, result, and retained failure reason; blocking dependencies recorded as SPECIFIC missing APIs/tests, never a broad "supported by Asupersync" assumption; a shipping composition selected from evidence (first host/client pair for Phase 1, transport profile go/no-go, browser bar coverage, identity metadata pinning, mic-endpoint per-OS status); NO row marked passed merely because source comments describe an intended implementation.

This gate feeds Phase 1 directly: the first complete controlled desktop is built only from spike-proven paths. Provenance: plan section 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 1 exit gate: one complete controlled desktop survives faults without stale authority
description:
WHY: The plan's first product milestone: one native host/client pair, end to end, correct under failure — with the generation model in from the beginning, not retrofitted.

EXIT CRITERIA (all with retained evidence): an actual interactive session survives media-worker restart, network interruption, client focus loss, stale-view/input-ticket expiry, and display resize with NO stale authority and NO growing queue; bootstrap/recovery works under modest real packet loss; basic rate control operates; optional local approval gates observation; origin protections exist for any exposed browser ingress; the instrumented latency result exists from the harness bead; a mock codec does NOT satisfy this gate — the real hardware path runs. The deterministic property suite is green, the fault list above is executed against the real process family, and results are revision-bound.

Closing this epic authorizes Phase 2 work. Provenance: plan section 23 Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] The fault list above is executed through the fr-e2e harness with retained artifact bundles; the fr-ffi wrapper passes its integration suite so the second (Windows/Linux) path stays close to the Apple path

title: Phase 2 exit gate: all host platforms + native desktop clients with device evidence
description:
WHY: Phase 2 completes the desktop product: three host adapters, native desktop clients, bidirectional audio where endpoints qualify, the shared clipboard, file send/receive, displays, viewers, discovery, diagnostics, and installers.

EXIT CRITERIA: the common session/input fault suite passes on EACH qualified OS with actual device evidence (kill/stall the worker during capture/encode/config-change/shutdown; disconnect Tailscale with modifiers held; crash the client; remove a display during a drag; change scale during a click; switch local user sessions during handoff; codec-device exhaustion degrades or refuses without a hidden CPU fallback; sleep/wake, cert renewal, tailnet switch, permission revocation, audio-device changes, expired/unknown peer metadata); packaging smoke tests pass per OS; the capability matrix rows for every host OS are filled with passed/failed/blocked/not-tested and exact versions; native GUI event loops integrate through the common Asupersync-owned machinery (no second runtime smuggled in via a shell).

Closing this epic authorizes Phase 3. Provenance: plan section 23 Phase 2, 24.2.

title: Phase 3 exit gate: real browsers and phones with no stale control preservable
description:
WHY: Phase 3 completes the client surface: browser and both mobile apps, connected through their own tailnet connectivity, with lifecycle rules that make stale authority impossible.

EXIT CRITERIA: real browser (Chrome and Safari per the v1.3 bar) and real phone clients connect through their OWN device tailnet connectivity — a browser is never a way to admit outside users through a gateway; background/resume, rotation, decoder pressure, and network changes cannot preserve stale control (device evidence from the mobile-qualification bead and the browser lifecycle tests); the capability matrix accurately separates supported, degraded (WSS), and unsupported combinations including audio-both-ways and file-transfer rows; origin security attack tests green; Asupersync's selected browser/mobile features qualified rather than trusted from preview labels.

Closing this epic authorizes Phase 4. Provenance: plan section 23 Phase 3.

title: Phase 4 exit gate: stable operating points, bounded queues, replayable decisions
description:
WHY: Phase 4 is where measured quality becomes a product property; its gate demands evidence, not vibes.

EXIT CRITERIA: the defined network scenarios show stable operating points with bounded application queueing (byte-asserted, not just counts); measured text/latency tradeoffs recorded per policy mode; controller decisions replay deterministically from sanitized traces; idle/settle-to-sharp behavior measured including first-frame-after-idle and last-frame-before-idle; folder-sync jobs correct under the conflict/soak tests; copy-optimization results retained.

Closing this epic authorizes Phase 5 release qualification. Provenance: plan section 23 Phase 4.

title: PROTOCOL.md v0: normative draft of messages, generations, roles, and limits
description:
WHY: fr-wire needs a written contract to implement, and the plan requires one concise wire specification with golden messages before v1 freezes. Drafting it first prevents the codec from becoming the accidental spec.

SCOPE: Replace the PROTOCOL.md stub with a v0 draft covering: version negotiation (protocol, robot schema, capability names, transport profile versioned separately); the message classes (Negotiation: ClientHello/HostCapabilities/SelectedConfiguration/Refused; Session: SessionOpened/ApprovalRequired/LeaseGranted/LeaseRevoked/Challenge/ChallengeResponse/InputTicket/ChannelAttach/Closed; Displays; Media: DecoderConfiguration/DecoderConfigured/RecoveryAccessUnit/FirstFrameDecoded/AccessUnitFragment/RepairRequest/RecoveryRequest; Input: KeyTransition/ButtonTransition/PointerState/RelativeCheckpoint/Scroll/CommitText/HeldState; Auxiliary: CursorShape/ClipboardBegin-Chunk-Commit/AudioConfiguration/AudioPacket/file-transfer envelope; Feedback: PresentedState/ReceiverPressure/StageMetrics/QualityDecision); byte order, field widths/varint choice, timestamp units, signed coordinates, max nesting; allowed sender role and state per message (a host can never send a host-input command a client would apply to its own OS); compact stream bindings for session/display/codec-config/recovery/viewport so datagrams reject stale work without repeating full tokens; the limits table referencing fr-core's single structure; fail-closed rules for unknown required flags and contradictory fragments.

ACCEPTANCE: every message names its sender role, size bound, and state constraints; limits match fr-core exactly; the doc marks itself v0-draft (frozen only by the Phase 5 freeze bead). Provenance: plan sections 7.2, 12.4, 17.

title: Optional opt-in software encoder profile: x265/oxideav-h265 evaluation behind the contracts
description:
WHY: The plan keeps a software encoder as a rescue/unsupported-hardware option — opt-in, visibly CPU-limited, negotiating lower geometry/frame-rate instead of silently consuming all cores — and names oxideav-h265 as a legitimate pure-Rust candidate to EVALUATE (its README claims an I/P/B encoder at 8-bit 4:2:0 with dimensions divisible by 16; claims are things to verify, not evidence). This bead preserves that feature without letting it touch the critical path.

SCOPE: (1) Define the opt-in software profile behind the fr-media contracts: explicit selection only (hardware-required deployments fail typed instead), enforced geometry/frame-rate ceilings, visible CPU-cost reporting in diagnostics. (2) Evaluate candidates at a pinned revision each: x265 (GPL/commercial licensing and patent considerations recorded — placing it in a plugin/process does NOT automatically settle redistribution; the shipped combination needs a recorded distribution decision) and oxideav-h265 (independent decoder interoperability, supported bitstream subset, adversarial-input behavior, throughput/memory/quality at matched bitrate, browser-target build sanity). (3) Write the adopt/defer/reject decision note with measurements.

CONSTRAINTS: no second runtime or large multimedia stack smuggled in; no uncapped optimization project; the replaceable media interface is the boundary; DECISION from the plan stands — no HEVC encoder written from scratch.

ACCEPTANCE: the evaluation report with retained runs and the licensing/distribution analysis; if adopted, the profile ships with its own capability row and CPU-envelope disclosure; if not, the negative evidence is recorded and the profile stays absent. Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 9.3, 9.4, 25.

title: Version 1 release: signed artifacts reproducing tested behavior
description:
WHY: The definition of done: install a small process family on a supported host already on Tailscale, grant OS permissions, and use the desktop from qualified native desktop, mobile, and browser clients — no account, no pairing — with every failure honest and every claim evidenced.

EXIT CRITERIA: signed/notarized macOS family, signed Windows packages, reproducible Linux package, mobile store-signed builds, browser assets versioned with the protocol — all built by repository-owned commands through the dsr lanes; installation artifacts reproduce the tested behavior (release-candidate re-run of the fault and security suites on the shipped binaries); unsupported states fail specifically; no performance claim outruns retained evidence; license/provenance manifests complete for every native component (FFmpeg configuration and license notices, opus, the Windows audio component, platform SDKs) with the distribution decision recorded; the v1.4 completion rules honored — expired input never executes, approval gates observation, shared encoders outlive subscribers, recovery works under the advertised loss envelope, browser idle/flush and endpoint-audio scopes have qualification evidence; codebase under the 240k ceiling by the fixed counting command.

Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 23 Phase 5, 26.

title: Workspace bootstrap: root Cargo.toml plus fr-core first slice (typed IDs, generations, limits)
description:
WHY: Everything else in the project consumes typed identifiers and one tested limits structure, and the cargo workspace cannot exist safely without its first real crate (a virtual workspace with zero members breaks every cargo command in the checkout — verified empirically before this tracker existed).

SCOPE: In ONE commit, create the root Cargo.toml (resolver "3", members = ["crates/*"], [workspace.package] edition 2024 + license-file, [workspace.dependencies] with asupersync pinned default-features=false and an fr-core path entry, workspace lints with unsafe_code = "forbid"), Cargo.lock, and crates/fr-core with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] as line 1. fr-core's first vertical slice: (a) distinct newtype identifiers for host boot, OS session, remote session, input lease, display geometry, codec configuration, recovery generation, and viewport mapping — deliberately NOT interchangeable, no raw u64s crossing module boundaries; (b) the single limits structure holding the protocol/resource ceilings: 64 KiB ordinary control message, 1 MiB clipboard item, 16 MiB max encoded access unit, 8192 max per axis, 16,777,216 max coded pixels, 2-12 picture reassembly window, 32 MiB per-viewer compressed budget — all as negotiate-downward ceilings with checked arithmetic helpers that validate length/stride/product before any allocation.

CONSTRAINTS: Asupersync is the only runtime dependency. No unsafe. Never leave a directory under crates/ without a manifest, even briefly.

ACCEPTANCE: cargo fmt/check/clippy/test green; unit tests prove identifier non-interchangeability (compile-fail tests where practical), ceiling validation rejects over-limit and overflow-adjacent values, and the limits structure round-trips its negotiated-downward logic. Provenance: plan sections 7.2, 17.2, 22.1; AGENTS.md section 8.1.

title: xtask: verification lanes and the one fixed line-counting command
description:
WHY: The plan requires repository-owned build/test commands as the authority (GitHub-hosted Actions is never the correctness contract) and ONE fixed counting command so the 194k-line budget is tracked identically at every milestone and never redefined near the end.

SCOPE: xtask (or extension of scripts/verify.sh) providing: fmt/check/clippy/test lanes per crate and workspace; the counting command reporting handwritten Rust, generated bindings, non-Rust glue (JS/Swift/Kotlin, 20k allowance), vendored source, and project-induced upstream changes as SEPARATE numbers; wiring so the dispatch-only workflow manifest and dsr/act call these commands verbatim.

CONSTRAINTS: no unique correctness logic in YAML; lanes that cannot run yet refuse honestly (exit nonzero with a dormant message) rather than reporting a pass.

ACCEPTANCE: counting output is stable and documented; verify lanes green on the current tree; a planted over-budget fixture demonstrates the count actually measures what it claims. Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 22.2; AGENTS.md section 10.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): a feature-resolved per-target dependency and unsafe audit lane (AGENTS sections 3.2/3.5, plan 19.1/20.1): for each build target (host desktop OSes, wasm32, mobile), resolve the actual feature graph and assert the target-specific rules — the browser build inherits no desktop FFI, the daemon inherits no GUI dependency, unsafe appears only in the named boundary crates, and direct/transitive/native/build-only/test-only dependencies are reported separately. A planted violation fixture (a test-only crate wrongly reachable from a shipping target) proves the lane catches drift.
